## Methanol as a Transition Fuel — Singapore EOI Findings

MPA's EOI for methanol as a marine fuel returned 50 submissions from "over 60 regional and international companies comprising energy companies, fuel suppliers, traders, bunker operators, and storage companies." Several projects in the submission pool were "already in operation or have crossed Final Investment Decision." On aggregate, "these projects have the potential to supply over one MTPA of low-carbon methanol by 2030, subject to commercial decisions and global developments." *Source: MPA — Singapore gears up to meet net-zero needs of shipping, MPA, 17 April 2024. https://www.mpa.gov.sg/media-centre/details/singapore-gears-up-to-meet-net-zero-needs-of-shipping.

*Analytical inference:* The concentration of methanol supply proposals at Singapore, combined with the scheduled delivery of methanol-capable Type II bunker tankers, positions Singapore as a near-term methanol bunkering hub for transpacific and Asia–Europe trade lanes. For workspaces whose ocean carriers operate on these lanes and have or are ordering methanol-dual-fuel vessels, Singapore is becoming the logical refuelling waypoint.

## IEA–MPA MOU on Energy Transition

MPA and the International Energy Agency (IEA) signed a Memorandum of Understanding "on the Energy Transition of the Maritime and Port Industries" at the April 2024 conference. The MOU covers sharing of best practices, support for zero and near-zero emission fuel adoption "through capacity building training programmes," and contribution to "relevant fuel-related projects and initiatives such as the IMO-Singapore NextGEN and NextGEN Connect Initiatives." It also supports "the development of the IEA Regional Cooperation Centre to be hosted by Singapore." *Source: MPA — Singapore gears up to meet net-zero needs of shipping, MPA, 17 April 2024. https://www.mpa.gov.sg/media-centre/details/singapore-gears-up-to-meet-net-zero-needs-of-shipping.

*Analytical inference:* The IEA–MPA MOU creates a channel for Singapore's maritime decarbonisation data to be incorporated into IEA energy transition modelling, which in turn feeds into OECD-level policy discourse. For workspaces whose clients or investors track IEA scenario outputs, Singapore's positioning within that analytical framework is a credibility signal.

## IMO–MPA NextGEN Initiative

The NextGEN initiative (where "GEN" stands for "Green and Efficient Navigation") is a joint IMO–MPA project cited by the IMO Secretary-General as an example of Singapore's support for ensuring "that the green and digital transition in maritime reaches all parts of the world, bringing on board Least Developed Countries and Small Island Developing States." *Source: MPA — Singapore gears up to meet net-zero needs of shipping, MPA, 17 April 2024. https://www.mpa.gov.sg/media-centre/details/singapore-gears-up-to-meet-net-zero-needs-of-shipping. No further operational detail on the NextGEN programme was available in the source pool.

The Green Ship Programme (GSP) sets out voluntary eligibility criteria under which SRS-registered ships and ocean-going vessels calling at the Port of Singapore may qualify for port dues and registration fee concessions. The programme is active from 1 January 2025 until 31 December 2027.

For SRS vessels, MPA provides "up to 100% concessions on initial registration fees and annual tonnage taxes" for vessels that:
- Exceed "IMO's MARPOL Annex VI Phase 3 Energy Efficiency Design Index (EEDI) requirements by 10% or more";
- Adopt "low-carbon fuelled engine";
- Adopt "zero-carbon coupled with near-zero emissions fuelled engine";
- Adopt "zero-emission fuelled engine/technology"; or
- Achieve "Carbon Intensity Indicator (CII) Rating A."

*Source: MPA — Maritime Singapore Green Initiative, MPA, 2024. https://www.mpa.gov.sg/maritime-singapore/sustainability/maritime-singapore-green-initiative.

For ocean-going vessels calling at the Port of Singapore, MPA provides "up to 100% port dues concession" to vessels using: zero-emission fuel/technology; zero-carbon fuel (e.g. ammonia, B100 biofuel, green methanol); low-carbon content fuels with CF value ≤ 1.375 (e.g. methanol) or LNG with methane slip addressed to max 1% or biofuels B50–B99; or low-carbon fuels with 1.375 < CF value ≤ 2.750, e.g. LNG without methane slip addressed or biofuels B24–B49. *Source: MPA — Maritime Singapore Green Initiative, MPA, 2024. https://www.mpa.gov.sg/maritime-singapore/sustainability/maritime-singapore-green-initiative.

*Operational implication:* For workspaces whose ocean carriers qualify for 100% port dues concession under the zero-emission or zero-carbon fuel tier, there is a quantifiable freight-cost advantage that may be passed through as lower port surcharges. For workspaces whose carriers do not qualify, the full port dues cost baseline applies through at least 31 December 2027.

*Analytical inference:* The detailed GSP criteria are further specified in Shipping Circular No. 12 of 2024 and Port Marine Circular No. 13 of 2024, referenced in the source block but not reproduced in full. Workspaces should retrieve these circulars directly from MPA's circulars registry for complete eligibility conditions.

## 7.1 Green Ship Programme — Incentive Criteria and Concession Structure

The Green Ship Programme (GSP) sets out voluntary eligibility criteria under which SRS-registered ships and ocean-going vessels calling at the Port of Singapore may qualify for port dues and registration fee concessions. The programme is active from 1 January 2025 until 31 December 2027.

For SRS vessels, MPA provides "up to 100% concessions on initial registration fees and annual tonnage taxes" for vessels that:
- Exceed "IMO's MARPOL Annex VI Phase 3 Energy Efficiency Design Index (EEDI) requirements by 10% or more";
- Adopt "low-carbon fuelled engine";
- Adopt "zero-carbon coupled with near-zero emissions fuelled engine";
- Adopt "zero-emission fuelled engine/technology"; or
- Achieve "Carbon Intensity Indicator (CII) Rating A."

*Source: MPA — Maritime Singapore Green Initiative, MPA, 2024. https://www.mpa.gov.sg/maritime-singapore/sustainability/maritime-singapore-green-initiative.

For ocean-going vessels calling at the Port of Singapore, MPA provides "up to 100% port dues concession" to vessels using: zero-emission fuel/technology; zero-carbon fuel (e.g. ammonia, B100 biofuel, green methanol); low-carbon content fuels with CF value ≤ 1.375 (e.g. methanol) or LNG with methane slip addressed to max 1% or biofuels B50–B99; or low-carbon fuels with 1.375 < CF value ≤ 2.750, e.g. LNG without methane slip addressed or biofuels B24–B49. *Source: MPA — Maritime Singapore Green Initiative, MPA, 2024. https://www.mpa.gov.sg/maritime-singapore/sustainability/maritime-singapore-green-initiative.

*Operational implication:* For workspaces whose ocean carriers qualify for 100% port dues concession under the zero-emission or zero-carbon fuel tier, there is a quantifiable freight-cost advantage that may be passed through as lower port surcharges. For workspaces whose carriers do not qualify, the full port dues cost baseline applies through at least 31 December 2027.

*Analytical inference:* The detailed GSP criteria are further specified in Shipping Circular No. 12 of 2024 and Port Marine Circular No. 13 of 2024, referenced in the source block but not reproduced in full. Workspaces should retrieve these circulars directly from MPA's circulars registry for complete eligibility conditions.

## 7.2 Green Craft Programme — Harbour Craft Incentives

The Green Craft Programme (GCP) encourages early adoption of zero-emission fuel, technology, and zero/low-carbon fuels for newbuild harbour craft. MPA provides "up to 100% port dues concession" for newbuild harbour craft registered from 1 January 2025 until 31 December 2027 that meet criteria for: use of low-carbon fuels; use of zero-carbon fuel; or use of zero-emission fuel/technology. *Source: MPA — Maritime Singapore Green Initiative, MPA, 2024. https://www.mpa.gov.sg/maritime-singapore/sustainability/maritime-singapore-green-initiative.

Craft previously registered under the Green Port Programme (GPP) continue to enjoy the 5-year waiver of craft port dues "until the end of 5-year validity period, or until 31 December 2027, whichever is earlier," provided the craft maintains its MPA licence and demonstrates use of qualifying fuel/technology throughout the year. *Source: MPA — Maritime Singapore Green Initiative, MPA, 2024. https://www.mpa.gov.sg/maritime-singapore/sustainability/maritime-singapore-green-initiative.

*Analytical inference:* The detailed GCP criteria are further specified in Port Marine Circular No. 15 of 2024, referenced in the source block but not reproduced in full.

## 7.3 Green Port Infrastructure Programme — Energy Efficiency Grant

The Energy Efficiency Grant (EEG) under the Green Port Infrastructure Programme (GPIP) "helps businesses transition towards being more energy efficient by co-funding their investments in energy efficient equipment." The EEG provides two tiers: a base tier supporting pre-approved energy-efficient equipment up to S$30,000; and an advanced tier for larger investments driving greater energy efficiency, with support capped at S$350,000 per company across both tiers. For the port sector, eligible companies can receive "up to 70% co-funding support for the adoption of energy efficient electric forklift(s) under the EEG (base tier)." The application window for the EEG base tier is until 31 March 2027. *Source: MPA — Maritime Singapore Green Initiative, MPA, 2024. https://www.mpa.gov.sg/maritime-singapore/sustainability/maritime-singapore-green-initiative.

## 7.4 Green Energy and Technology Programme

The Green Energy and Technology Programme (GETP) "aims to encourage Singapore-based maritime companies to develop and/or conduct pilot trials for green technologies that can help vessels meet the 2023 IMO Strategy on Reduction of GHG Emissions from Ships targets." *Source: MPA — Maritime Singapore Green Initiative, MPA, 2024. https://www.mpa.gov.sg/maritime-singapore/sustainability/maritime-singapore-green-initiative.

*Analytical inference:* The GETP is the most directly relevant incentive programme for workspaces or their supply-chain partners that are evaluating green technology pilot participation in Singapore. No further detail on GETP eligibility criteria, application processes, or funding quantum was available in the source pool.

## 7.5 Green Awareness Programme — Carbon Management MOU

The Green Awareness Programme (GAP) "will focus on raising awareness on and developing industry capabilities in carbon accounting and management." It is "primarily driven by efforts under the Carbon Management Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) signed between MPA, the United Nations Global Compact Network Singapore (GCNS), and various industry associations, including the Association of Regional Ferry Operators (ARFO), the Association of Singapore Marine Industries." *Source: MPA — Maritime Singapore Green Initiative, MPA, 2024. https://www.mpa.gov.sg/maritime-singapore/sustainability/maritime-singapore-green-initiative.

*Analytical inference:* For workspaces seeking to build credible carbon accounting capability for Singapore port operations — relevant to Scope 3 emissions disclosure under frameworks such as ISO 14083 or CSRD — the GAP and the Carbon Management MOU represent a direct engagement channel with MPA and Singapore-based industry associations.

## 7.6 Methanol Bunkering Development — Market Signal

MPA received 50 submissions in response to its Expression of Interest for methanol as a marine fuel in Singapore. MPA noted that "the demand for methanol as a marine fuel in Singapore can potentially exceed one million tons per annum (MTPA) before 2030, subject to the pace of developments of supply chains, infrastructure, and regulations globally." The EOI covered three areas: methanol supply, methanol bunkering operating model at commercial scale, and alternatives to physical transfer of methanol molecules to Singapore. Approximately 40% of submissions proposed "end-to-end solutions covering all three areas." *Source: MPA — Singapore gears up to meet net-zero needs of shipping, MPA, 17 April 2024. https://www.mpa.gov.sg/media-centre/details/singapore-gears-up-to-meet-net-zero-needs-of-shipping.

*Analytical inference:* For workspaces whose contracted ocean carriers have ordered or are considering methanol-dual-fuel vessels, Singapore's methanol bunkering development trajectory directly affects route feasibility. The "scheduled delivery of Type II bunker tankers capable of supplying methanol" described in the source for 2024 indicates that Singapore is actively building methanol bunkering capacity, making Singapore-routed methanol bunkering commercially viable on a shortening horizon.

## 7.7 IMO 2023 GHG Strategy Checkpoint Targets

The IMO 2023 GHG Strategy sets "indicative checkpoints to reach by 2030 (cut GHG emissions by at least 20%, striving for 30%), and 2040 (cut GHG emissions by at least 70%, striving for 80%). The targets are for the entire shipping sector." Singapore's Blueprint and implementing instruments are explicitly framed as contributing to these IMO checkpoint targets. *Source: MPA — Singapore gears up to meet net-zero needs of shipping, MPA, 17 April 2024. https://www.mpa.gov.sg/media-centre/details/singapore-gears-up-to-meet-net-zero-needs-of-shipping.

*Specific penalty / enforcement provision not available from primary sources at the time of this authoring pass.* The source pool does not contain a penalty schedule or enforcement mechanism for non-compliance with any specific Blueprint-derived mandate. This gap applies across Sections 7.1 through 7.7.

**MONITORING — IMO Mid-Term Measures (Goal-Based Marine Fuel Standard + GHG Pricing Mechanism)**

IMO Secretary-General Arsenio Dominguez, speaking at the MPA Accelerating Digitalisation and Decarbonisation Conference in April 2024, stated that mid-term measures — comprising "a goal-based marine fuel standard, and a pricing mechanism for maritime GHG emissions" — were "currently being discussed by Member States" and that the IMO was "on track to adopt mid-term measures by late 2025." *Source: MPA — Singapore gears up to meet net-zero needs of shipping, MPA, 17 April 2024. https://www.mpa.gov.sg/media-centre/details/singapore-gears-up-to-meet-net-zero-needs-of-shipping.

*Analytical inference:* Adoption of IMO mid-term measures (if they proceeded on the stated 2025 schedule or are progressing into 2026) would be the single highest-consequence upstream trigger for Singapore's implementing instruments, because MPA has consistently framed its regulatory trajectory as aligned with IMO milestones. The workspace should re-check the IMO MEPC docket (MEPC 83 and subsequent sessions) for adoption status. Re-check window: Q3 2026.

**MONITORING — Methanol Bunkering Regulatory Framework**

MPA stated that EOI submissions received would "inform the development of the methanol bunkering regulatory framework to ensure the safe and efficient supply of methanol." The framework is explicitly described as under development, not yet published. *Source: MPA — Singapore gears up to meet net-zero needs of shipping, MPA, 17 April 2024. https://www.mpa.gov.sg/media-centre/details/singapore-gears-up-to-meet-net-zero-needs-of-shipping.

*Analytical inference:* Given that MPA received 50 EOI submissions in early 2024 and described demand potentially exceeding one million tons per annum before 2030, the methanol bunkering regulatory framework is likely to be published in the 2025–2027 window. Exact publication date not available from sources. Re-check window: Q4 2026.

**MONITORING — MSGI Strategy Review**

MPA has stated it "constantly refines and reviews our strategies and initiatives" and will provide "periodic updates to the industry at relevant fora." No specific date for the next review has been identified in the source pool. *Source: MPA — Maritime Singapore Decarbonisation Blueprint, MPA, 2022. https://www.mpa.gov.sg/maritime-singapore/sustainability/maritime-singapore-decarbonisation-blueprint.

*Analytical inference:* The MSGI was last refreshed in 2024; a further refresh may occur as IMO mid-term measures are adopted and as Singapore approaches 2030 checkpoint targets. Re-check window: Q2 2027 (end of current MSGI programme windows).

**MONITORING — Ammonia Bunkering Capability Development**

MPA CEO Teo Eng Dih stated at the April 2024 conference that "MPA is working with stakeholders to develop pathways for these marine fuels, especially in areas of provision of necessary infrastructure, crew training, regulations, and safety standards for bunkering of such fuels." Ammonia bunkering is explicitly named alongside methanol. No published ammonia bunkering regulatory framework was identified in the source pool. *Source: MPA — Singapore gears up to meet net-zero needs of shipping, MPA, 17 April 2024. https://www.mpa.gov.sg/media-centre/details/singapore-gears-up-to-meet-net-zero-needs-of-shipping.

## What This Instrument Is

The Maritime Singapore Decarbonisation Blueprint: Working Towards 2050 is a strategic policy document published in 2022 by the Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore (MPA). It is not a single binding regulation but a coordinating framework that organises Singapore's maritime decarbonisation commitments into seven focus areas and underpins a suite of implementing instruments — among them the Maritime Singapore Green Initiative (MSGI) and its sub-programmes — which carry specific incentive structures, eligibility criteria, and deadlines that are actionable for operators.

The Blueprint "charts ambitious and concrete long-term strategies to build a sustainable Maritime Singapore" and was "developed by the Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore (MPA) in consultation with industry partners." *Source: MPA — Maritime Singapore Decarbonisation Blueprint, MPA, 2022. https://www.mpa.gov.sg/maritime-singapore/sustainability/maritime-singapore-decarbonisation-blueprint.

The Blueprint commits to contributions toward "Singapore's commitments under the United Nations' 2030 Sustainable Development Agenda, Paris Agreement and the Initial IMO Strategy on reduction of GHG emissions from ships." *Source: MPA — Maritime Singapore Decarbonisation Blueprint, MPA, 2022. https://www.mpa.gov.sg/maritime-singapore/sustainability/maritime-singapore-decarbonisation-blueprint.

The Blueprint "outlines seven focus areas, which MPA will focus on to support the decarbonisation of the maritime industry: Port terminals; Domestic harbour craft; Future marine fuels, bunkering standards and infrastructure; Singapore Registry of Ships; Efforts at IMO and other international platforms; Research & development and talent; and Carbon awareness, carbon accounting and green financing." *Source: MPA — Maritime Singapore Decarbonisation Blueprint, MPA, 2022. https://www.mpa.gov.sg/maritime-singapore/sustainability/maritime-singapore-decarbonisation-blueprint.

"Given the dynamic developments in the global maritime decarbonisation landscape, MPA constantly refines and reviews our strategies and initiatives to ensure alignment with our local and global net-zero targets. Periodic updates will continue to be provided to the industry at relevant fora." *Source: MPA — Maritime Singapore Decarbonisation Blueprint, MPA, 2022. https://www.mpa.gov.sg/maritime-singapore/sustainability/maritime-singapore-decarbonisation-blueprint.

## Why It Applies to the Workspace

*Analytical inference:* For workspaces whose air-primary freight operations use Singapore Changi as a hub and whose ocean-mode shipments transit or originate at the Port of Singapore — one of the world's highest-volume bunkering and transhipment ports — the Blueprint's implementing instruments create direct cost and compliance touch points. The MSGI's Green Ship Programme and Green Craft Programme set port dues concession eligibility criteria that affect which vessels call at Singapore and at what cost; the methanol and ammonia bunkering framework development affects fuel optionality for ocean carriers serving Singapore routes; and the harbour craft mandate (addressed in Section 8 below) affects the craft operators who handle port-side logistics for the workspace's cargo.

*Analytical inference:* Workspaces that charter or contract ocean carriers flagged on the Singapore Registry of Ships (SRS) face indirect exposure: SRS-registered vessels are the primary target population for the Green Ship Programme's fee concessions and future mandatory requirements, which over time shape the fleet composition and fuel cost structure of Singapore-flagged carriers.

*Analytical inference:* Workspaces that use Singapore as a primary ocean transhipment node for Asia–Americas or Asia–Europe lanes will find that port-call costs for their contracted carriers are partially determined by whether those carriers qualify for MSGI port dues concessions, making carrier sustainability certification a commercial variable, not only a reporting one.

**Effective date:** The Blueprint was published in 2022. The MSGI was refreshed and the current S$50 million commitment announced in 2024. Specific programme windows (Green Ship Programme, Green Craft Programme) run from 1 January 2025 until 31 December 2027. *Source: MPA — Maritime Singapore Green Initiative, MPA, 2024. https://www.mpa.gov.sg/maritime-singapore/sustainability/maritime-singapore-green-initiative.

**Jurisdictional scope:** The Blueprint and its implementing instruments apply within Singapore's port jurisdiction, to Singapore-registered ships (SRS), to ocean-going vessels calling at the Port of Singapore, and to MPA-licensed harbour craft operating in Singapore waters. *Source: MPA — Maritime Singapore Green Initiative, MPA, 2024. https://www.mpa.gov.sg/maritime-singapore/sustainability/maritime-singapore-green-initiative.

*Specific penalty / enforcement provision not available from primary sources at the time of this authoring pass.* The source pool does not contain a penalty schedule or enforcement mechanism for non-compliance with Blueprint-derived mandates. This is flagged as a required research gap (see Section 3 and the Confirmed Regulatory Timeline).

---

**MONITORING** — Green Ship Programme and Green Craft Programme windows are open now (1 January 2025 – 31 December 2027): workspaces whose contracted ocean carriers or harbour craft operators may qualify for port dues concessions under the MSGI should confirm their carriers' eligibility status against the published criteria before contract renewals. Carriers that qualify receive up to 100% port dues concession; those that do not carry the full port dues cost. *Source: MPA — Maritime Singapore Green Initiative, MPA, 2024. https://www.mpa.gov.sg/maritime-singapore/sustainability/maritime-singapore-green-initiative.

**MONITORING** — Methanol bunkering regulatory framework under development: MPA received 50 EOI submissions for methanol supply as a marine fuel in Singapore and stated that "insights from the EOI submissions will inform the development of the methanol bunkering regulatory framework." The regulatory framework is not yet finalised in the source pool. Workspaces moving cargo on methanol-capable vessels through Singapore should track this framework's publication. *Source: MPA — Singapore gears up to meet net-zero needs of shipping, MPA, 17 April 2024. https://www.mpa.gov.sg/media-centre/details/singapore-gears-up-to-meet-net-zero-needs-of-shipping.

**MONITORING** — IMO mid-term measures (goal-based marine fuel standard and GHG pricing mechanism) were described at the April 2024 conference as being "currently being discussed by Member States" with adoption targeted by "late 2025." These measures, when adopted, will cascade into Singapore's implementing instruments. *Legal Confirmation Required:* the precise interaction between adopted IMO measures and Singapore's domestic implementing framework — including which MPA instruments will be amended and on what timeline — requires legal and regulatory confirmation once the IMO instruments are published in final form. *Source: MPA — Singapore gears up to meet net-zero needs of shipping, MPA, 17 April 2024. https://www.mpa.gov.sg/media-centre/details/singapore-gears-up-to-meet-net-zero-needs-of-shipping.

**WINDOW CLOSING** — Energy Efficiency Grant (EEG) base tier application window closes 31 March 2027: port-sector operators eligible for up to 70% co-funding for energy-efficient electric forklifts under the MSGI Green Port Infrastructure Programme should confirm eligibility and submit before this date. *Source: MPA — Maritime Singapore Green Initiative, MPA, 2024. https://www.mpa.gov.sg/maritime-singapore/sustainability/maritime-singapore-green-initiative.

*Specific penalty / enforcement provision not available from primary sources at the time of this authoring pass.* No penalty schedule for non-compliance with Blueprint-derived mandates was retrievable from the source pool. Identifying the enforcement mechanism is itself an immediate action for workspaces with material Singapore port exposure.

---

## System Requirements for Workspaces Directly Engaging MSGI Programmes

**CII Rating Monitoring (if carriers are SRS-flagged):** *Analytical inference:* Workspaces whose contracted carriers are SRS-flagged and claim GSP concessions based on CII Rating A will need to track CII performance data from those carriers, because CII rating is a dynamic annual metric (calculated under MARPOL Annex VI) that must be maintained each year of the concession period. Workspaces that include CII data in sustainability reporting or client disclosures should ensure their carrier data collection processes capture annual CII rating, not just a one-time certification.

**Fuel Type Verification (for port dues concession claims):** *Analytical inference:* The GSP's port dues concession tiers are fuel-specific (zero-emission, zero-carbon, low-carbon with CF thresholds). For workspaces that pass through port dues surcharges to clients or report carrier fuel consumption under Scope 3 frameworks, the ability to verify which fuel tier a carrier used on a given port call is an operational data requirement. The source pool does not specify a MPA-issued verification mechanism for fuel type at port call; this is a research gap.

**GCP Craft Demonstration (for harbour craft operators):** Harbour craft operators registered under the GCP must "successfully demonstrate the use of zero-emission fuel/technology or zero/low carbon fuel throughout the year" and provide "calculations and verified proof of mitigation technologies." *Source: MPA — Maritime Singapore Green Initiative, MPA, 2024. https://www.mpa.gov.sg/maritime-singapore/sustainability/maritime-singapore-green-initiative. *Analytical inference:* For workspaces that manage or contract MPA-licensed harbour craft, this creates a metering and documentation obligation that is operationally distinct from the incentive application process.

**Carbon Accounting Capability (GAP / Carbon Management MOU):** *Analytical inference:* The Blueprint's seventh focus area ("Carbon awareness, carbon accounting and green financing") and the GAP programme signal that MPA expects Singapore-based maritime companies to develop internal carbon accounting capabilities over the Blueprint horizon. For workspaces with material Singapore port operations, building a carbon accounting baseline for port-related activities — covering Scope 1 (owned/operated craft), Scope 2 (electricity at terminal), and Scope 3 (contracted ocean carriers) — would be the foundational system requirement for participating in future MPA reporting or incentive programmes.

*Gap: no specific system architecture, data format, or software requirement has been mandated under the Blueprint or MSGI at the time of this authoring pass, per the source pool.*

---

The Blueprint and its implementing instruments create obligations and incentives across multiple layers of the maritime supply chain. The workspace's position in this chain depends on its transaction-by-transaction role.

**As freight forwarder / non-vessel operating carrier (NVOCC):** *Analytical inference:* Workspaces operating as freight forwarders or NVOCCs are not the direct target of vessel-level obligations (EEDI, CII, fuel mandates) — those obligations fall on the vessel owner or operator. However, the workspace is exposed through the commercial consequences: carriers qualifying for MSGI concessions price their port calls differently from those that do not, and those cost differences may or may not be passed through to freight rates and surcharges.

**As shipper / importer / exporter:** *Analytical inference:* Workspaces that place cargo on vessels calling at the Port of Singapore are indirectly exposed through their carriers' compliance posture. Carriers with CII Rating A or zero-emission fuel qualification receive port dues concessions; carriers without them bear higher port costs, which over time flow into freight pricing.

**As a cargo principal using harbour craft services in Singapore waters:** *Analytical inference:* Port-side logistics for cargo transiting Singapore — including lightering, ship-to-shore transfer, and terminal operations — rely on MPA-licensed harbour craft. The Green Craft Programme's mandate trajectory (see Section 8) means the craft operators serving the workspace's cargo are subject to phased fuel and technology mandates.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether any carbon accounting or green financing reporting obligation under the Blueprint's seventh focus area ("Carbon awareness, carbon accounting and green financing") applies to freight forwarders, shippers, or NVOCCs operating in Singapore — as distinct from vessel operators and port operators — requires legal confirmation against the specific implementing instruments published under that focus area.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* the Singapore Registry of Ships (SRS) focus area creates obligations on shipowners and operators of SRS-flagged vessels. Whether the workspace, in any of its transaction roles, has obligations as a ship manager or technical operator under SRS flag-state requirements is a role-specific legal question requiring counsel review.

*Source for this section: MPA — Maritime Singapore Decarbonisation Blueprint, MPA, 2022. https://www.mpa.gov.sg/maritime-singapore/sustainability/maritime-singapore-decarbonisation-blueprint; MPA — Maritime Singapore Green Initiative, MPA, 2024. https://www.mpa.gov.sg/maritime-singapore/sustainability/maritime-singapore-green-initiative.

---

This brief synthesises publicly available source content across five retrievable source blocks to characterise the Maritime Singapore Decarbonisation Blueprint (published 2022) and its associated implementation instruments, including the Maritime Singapore Green Initiative (MSGI, refreshed 2024). The primary source URL returned a 404 error; the substantive content below is drawn entirely from the four successfully retrieved MPA source pages and one MPA media release. The MOT source (https://www.mot.gov.sg/what-we-do/green-transport/maritime-environment-responsibility/) returned HTTP 403 (blocked); no content from that source is used in any FACT claim. The IEA policy tracker page (https://www.iea.org/policies/28030-maritime-singapore-green-initiative-msgi) returned a bot-verification wall; no content from that source is used in any FACT claim. Both are listed under New Sources Identified as leads for future retrieval.

**Conventions:** Inline citations follow each subsection. All FACT claims are span-grounded verbatim from retrieved source blocks. ANALYSIS claims are prefixed with a closed-set label token. Items requiring legal review carry *Legal Confirmation Required:* callouts. The workspace is referenced by operational profile throughout; no entity name appears.

**Scope limitation:** The primary source URL intended for this brief (https://mpa.gov.sg/media-centre/details/mpa-releases-detailed-implementation-plan-for-maritime-decarbonisation) resolved to a 404 page. No implementation plan detail was retrievable from that URL. This brief therefore characterises the Blueprint as a strategic framework and incentive architecture rather than a granular implementation regulation. Where a specific implementing regulation is referenced but its full text is not in the source pool, this is flagged as a research gap.

**Date of generation:** current as of this authoring pass.

---

## Registration

**Green Ship Programme:** Singapore-registered ship owners and operators of ocean-going vessels calling at the Port of Singapore that wish to claim GSP concessions are directed to Shipping Circular No. 12 of 2024 and Port Marine Circular No. 13 of 2024 for registration and application procedures. These circulars are referenced in the source block but their full text is not in the source pool. *Source: MPA — Maritime Singapore Green Initiative, MPA, 2024. https://www.mpa.gov.sg/maritime-singapore/sustainability/maritime-singapore-green-initiative.

**Green Craft Programme:** Harbour craft operators applying for GCP port dues concessions are directed to Port Marine Circular No. 15 of 2024 for registration procedures. *Source: MPA — Maritime Singapore Green Initiative, MPA, 2024. https://www.mpa.gov.sg/maritime-singapore/sustainability/maritime-singapore-green-initiative.

**Energy Efficiency Grant (GPIP base tier):** Applications are submitted through the GoBusiness Singapore website. The application window is until 31 March 2027. *Source: MPA — Maritime Singapore Green Initiative, MPA, 2024. https://www.mpa.gov.sg/maritime-singapore/sustainability/maritime-singapore-green-initiative.

**Carbon Management MOU (GAP):** The MOU is signed between MPA, GCNS, and named industry associations. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether freight forwarders or cargo principals operating through Singapore can become signatories or obtain formal recognition under this MOU — and what reporting obligations attach to signatories — requires direct inquiry with MPA and GCNS.

## Reporting

*Specific reporting format and submission schedule for Blueprint-implementing instruments not available from primary sources at the time of this authoring pass.* The source pool confirms that GCP craft recipients must "provide MPA with documents including calculations and verified proof of mitigation technologies to continue to enjoy port dues waiver for the full 5-year validity period." Beyond this provision, the specific reporting formats, submission timelines, and data requirements for each MSGI programme are not detailed in the source pool. Retrieval of the implementing circulars (Shipping Circular No. 12/2024, Port Marine Circulars No. 13/2024 and No. 15/2024) is required to complete this section.

*Source: MPA — Maritime Singapore Green Initiative, MPA, 2024. https://www.mpa.gov.sg/maritime-singapore/sustainability/maritime-singapore-green-initiative.

The Maritime Singapore Decarbonisation Blueprint: Working Towards 2050 charts ambitious and concrete long-term strategies to build a sustainable Maritime Singapore. Developed by the Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore (MPA) in consultation with industry partners, the Blueprint will contribute to Singapore’s commitments under the United Nations’ 2030 Sustainable Development Agenda, Paris Agreement and the Initial IMO Strategy on reduction of GHG emissions from ships, and strengthen our value proposition as a leading global hub port and international maritime centre.    This Blueprint takes on board the recommendations made by the International Advisory Panel on Maritime Decarbonisation, and inputs from a two-month long public consultation and sector-specific consultations.   The Blueprint, published in 2022, outlines seven focus areas, which MPA will focus on to support the decarbonisation of the maritime industry: Port terminals; Domestic harbour craft; Future marine fuels, bunkering standards and infrastructure; Singapore Registry of Ships; Efforts at IMO and other international platforms; Research & development and talent; and Carbon awareness, carbon accounting and green financing. Given the dynamic developments in the global maritime decarbonisation landscape, MPA constantly refines and reviews our strategies and initiatives to ensure alignment with our local and global net-zero targets. Periodic updates will continue to be provided to the industry at relevant fora. Download the Maritime Singapore Decarbonisation Blueprint  here . Close notification Home > Maritime Singapore > Sustainability > Maritime Singapore Green Initiative > Maritime Singapore Green Initiative Maritime Singapore Green Initiative Maritime Singapore Decarbonisation Blueprint Share: Share to LinkedIn Share to Facebook Share to Twitter Print this page Share to Email Maritime Singapore Green Initiative The Maritime Singapore Green Initiative (MSGI) seeks to reduce the environmental impact of shipping and related activities and to promote clean and green shipping in Singapore. In 2011, the Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore (MPA) pledged to invest up to S$100 million over 5 years in the MSGI. Enhancements to the MSGI were made in 2013, 2019 and 2022, to further encourage companies to adopt environmentally friendly shipping practices. In 2024, MPA updated various green initiatives and incentives under the MSGI to encourage early adoption of zero and near-zero emission technologies and fuels. MPA will commit another S$50 million to support the implementation of the refreshed MSGI which comprises of five programmes: Green Ship Programme Green Port Infrastructure Programme Green Craft Programme Green Energy and Technology Programme Green Awareness Programme These are voluntary programmes designed to recognise and provide incentives to companies that adopt clean and green shipping practices and port operations. The initiative underscores Singapore's commitment as a responsible flag and port state to clean and green shipping.   Green Ship Programme The GSP provides incentives to Singapore-registered ships (SRS) and ocean-going vessels calling at the Port of Singapore that voluntarily adopt solutions that enable ships to exceed environmental regulatory standards set by the IMO. From 1 January 2025 until 31 December 2027, MPA will provide up to 100% concessions on initial registration fees and annual tonnage taxes for SRS which: Exceed International Maritime Organization’s (IMO) MARPOL Annex VI Phase 3 Energy Efficiency Design Index (EEDI) requirements by 10% or more; Adopt low-carbon fuelled engine; Adopt zero-carbon coupled with near-zero emissions fuelled engine; Adopt zero-emission fuelled engine/technology; or Achieve Carbon Intensity Indicator (CII) Rating A. From 1 January 2025 until 31 December 2027, MPA will provide up to 100% port dues concession to ocean-going vessels calling at the Port of Singapore which: Use of zero-emission fuel/technology (e.g. hydrogen, full electrification, hybrid of hydrogen fuel cell and electrification etc.); Use of zero-carbon fuel (e.g. ammonia with pilot fuel capped at 25% with ammonia slip/NO x /N 2 O addressed, B100 biofuel, green methanol etc.); Use of low-carbon content fuels with CF value ≤ 1.375 (e.g. methanol), or using LNG in engine with methane slip addressed to max 1%, or biofuels B50 and above up to B99; or Use of low carbon content fuels with 1.375 < CF value ≤ 2.750, e.g. LNG (in engine without methane slip addressed), or biofuels B24 and above up to B49. Please refer to the  Shipping Circular No. 12 of 2024  and Port Marine Circular No. 13 of 2024 for more information on the GSP. Green Port Programme The GPIP is a new programme that was included in MSGI in 2024. It supports the port’s net zero transition, primarily through fuel switch, energy optimisation and renewables generation. To support businesses in their sustainability journey, the Energy Efficiency Grant (EEG) helps businesses transition towards being more energy efficient by co-funding their investments in energy efficient equipment. The EEG provides two tiers of support – a base tier to provide support for pre-approved energy efficient equipment up to S$30,000; and an advanced tier to support companies for larger investments that drive greater energy efficiency. Support is capped at S$350,000 per company across base and advanced tiers. For the port sector, eligible companies can receive up to 70% co-funding support for the adoption of energy efficient electric forklift(s) under the EEG (base tier). The application window for the EEG (base tier) is until 31 March 2027. Please refer to the GoBusiness Singapore website for more information.  Green Craft Programme Port Dues Concession Under the revised MSGI, the port dues concessions for newbuild harbour craft under the Green Port Programme (GPP) will be subsumed under the new GCP, which encourages the early adoption of zero-emission fuel and technologies, as well as zero- and low- carbon fuels for newbuild harbour craft. All craft that are currently registered under the 5-year waiver of craft port dues for low or zero carbon-fuelled and fully electric MPA licensed harbour craft under the GPP will continue to enjoy the waiver of craft port dues until the end of 5-year validity period, or until 31 December 2027, whichever is earlier, provided that the craft (a) maintains the MPA licence, and (b) successfully demonstrates the use of zero-emission fuel/technology or zero/low carbon fuel throughout the year. For those craft that have yet to reach the full 5-year validity period as at 31 December 2027, they will also need to provide MPA with documents including calculations and verified proof of mitigation technologies to continue to enjoy port dues waiver for the full 5-year validity period, to be in line with GCP. The craft registered under the GPP will not be eligible for the new GCP.  For newbuild harbour craft registered from 1 January 2025 until 31 December 2027, MPA will provide up to 100% port dues concession that meet one of the criteria listed below: Use of low-carbon fuels; Use of zero-carbon fuel; or Use of zero-emission fuel/technology. Please refer to the  Port Marine Circular No. 15 of 2024  for more information on the GCP. Green Energy and Technology Programme The GETP aims to encourage Singapore-based maritime companies to develop and / or conduct pilot trials for green technologies that can help vessels meet the  2023 IMO Strategy on Reduction of GHG Emissions from Ships targets.  Green Awareness Programme The GAP will focus on raising awareness on and developing industry capabilities in carbon accounting and management. This will be primarily driven by efforts under the Carbon Management Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) signed between MPA, the United Nations Global Compact Network Singapore (GCNS), and various industry associations, including the Association of Regional Ferry Operators (ARFO), the Association of Singapore Marine Industries (ASMI), the Singapore Association of Ship Supplies and Services (SASS), and the Singapore Shipping Association (SSA). The key initiatives under the MoU are as follow. MPA will co-fund 50% of the fees payable for the carbon management workshops. Maritime SG LowCarbon50 Programme – This includes training workshops on carbon accounting and managements, and sharing on relevant initiatives, schemes, and technologies. Maritime SG LowCarbon50 Awards – This aims to recognize companies that have actively and accurately done carbon accounting, and that have clear effective emission reduction / management measurements in place.   To Top Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore Download myMaritime@SG Instagram Facebook X Youtube Linkedin Tiktok Report Vulnerability Privacy Statement Terms of Use Sitemap Contact Info Feedback RSS ©2026 Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore Last Updated on 09 Jun 2026

Close notification Singapore gears up to meet net-zero needs of shipping Published 17 Apr 2024 Share: Share to LinkedIn Share to Facebook Share to Twitter Print this page Share to Email      More than 500 participants from the industry, academia and international organisations gathered at the Accelerating Digitalisation and Decarbonisation Conference to discuss how value-chain stakeholders can work together to produce, transport, and bunker net-zero fuels safely, explore promising digital and data technology and solutions to decarbonise the maritime industry, and seed opportunities for collaboration on pilots and trials. The Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore (MPA) updated participants on Singapore’s methanol and ammonia bunkering capability developments, and net-zero pathways for the domestic harbour craft sector. The 3rd MaritimeSG LowCarbon50 Awards ceremony was also held during the event. 2.   Speaking at the conference, Mr Teo Eng Dih, Chief Executive, MPA said, “As an international maritime centre and global hub port, Singapore will work with our tripartite partners and international shipping community to digitalise, enhance energy efficiency, and deploy low and zero-carbon emission marine fuels. MPA is working with stakeholders to develop pathways for these marine fuels, especially in areas of provision of necessary infrastructure, crew training, regulations, and safety standards for bunkering of such fuels. A key priority is to establish the end-to-end value chains for these new fuels.” 3.   In his opening address, International Maritime Organization (IMO) Secretary-General Arsenio Dominguez highlighted the concrete steps taken by IMO Member States following the landmark adoption of the 2023 IMO Strategy on Reduction of GHG Emissions from Ships. Mr Dominguez said, “The IMO 2023 GHG Strategy demonstrates the shared commitment of Member States and the global shipping industry. We are on track to adopt mid-term measures by late 2025 to cut GHG emissions, to reach net zero targets. These mid-term measures, which are currently being discussed by Member States, include a goal-based marine fuel standard, and a pricing mechanism for maritime GHG emissions. These will help us progress towards achieving net-zero GHG emissions by or around 2050, with indicative checkpoints to reach by 2030 (cut GHG emissions by at least 20%, striving for 30%), and 2040 (cut GHG emissions by at least 70%, striving for 80%). The targets are for the entire shipping sector.” 4.   At the Marine Environment Protection Committee (MEPC 80) in July 2023, Singapore had worked actively with the IMO and other Member States to forge consensus in the adoption of the 2023 Strategy for the Reduction of GHG emissions from ships. Mr Dominguez thanked Singapore for its support to ensuring that the green and digital transition in maritime reaches all parts of the world, bringing on board LeastDeveloped Countries and Small Island Developing States. Specific projects include the joint IMO- MPA NextGEN initiative 1  (where “GEN” stands for “Green and Efficient Navigation”) and the IMO-Singapore Single Window for Facilitation of Trade (SWiFT) project 2 . 5.   MPA and the International Energy Agency (IEA) signed an MoU on the Energy Transition of the Maritime and Port Industries and announced the partnership at the event. The MoU will enable the sharing of best practices across maritime and energy industries, support the adoption and transition of zero and near-zero emission fuels by these industries through capacity building training programmes, and contribute to relevant fuel-related projects and initiatives such as the IMO-Singapore NextGEN and NextGEN Connect Initiatives. This will support the development of the IEA Regional Cooperation Centre to be hosted by Singapore. IEA Chief Economist, Mr Tim Gould, shared that the IEA warmly welcomes this MoU as a major step forward in their cooperation with the MPA, a critical player in the region and the world, to improve access to low-emission fuels. 50 proposals for the supply of methanol as a bunker fuel in Singapore. 6.   Following the completion of the world’s first ship-to-containership methanol bunkering in Singapore last year, MPA launched an expression of interest (EOI 3 ) for the supply of methanol as a marine fuel in Singapore. The EOI sought proposals covering three areas; methanol supply, methanol bunkering operating model at commercial scale, and alternatives to the physical transfer of methanol molecules to Singapore, to enable a resilient fuel supply to meet the needs of methanol-capable vessels in Singapore in the coming years. Based on consultations with the industry, the demand for methanol as a marine fuel in Singapore can potentially exceed one million tons per annum (MTPA) before 2030, subject to the pace of developments of supply chains, infrastructure, and regulations globally. 7.   There was strong interest in the EOI. MPA received a total of 50 submissions, out of which 40% of them proposed end-to-end solutions covering all three areas highlighted in the EOI. Over 60 regional and international companies comprising energy companies, fuel suppliers, traders, bunker operators, and storage companies, participated in the EOI, signalling clear business confidence in Singapore as a key offtake location for methanol by international shipping. 8.   The proposals received for the low carbon methanol supply and delivery are promising, with several projects already in operation or have crossed Final Investment Decision. On aggregate, these projects have the potential to supply over one MTPA of low-carbon methanol by 2030, subject to commercial decisions and global developments. Many of the companies plan to use ready storage infrastructure in Singapore and will partner craft operators to build or procure bunker tankers capable of carrying and delivering methanol, taking into consideration MPA’s safety and quality assurance standards, crew training requirements, and methanol bunker tanker specifications. The proposals received provide strong indications that the industry is preparing for methanol bunker demand to scale up in the coming years, most notably seen in the scheduled delivery of Type II bunker tankers capable of supplying methanol this year. 9.   Insights from the EOI submissions will inform the development of the methanol bunkering regulatory framework to ensure the safe and efficient supply of methanol as a marine fuel in Singapore at a commercial scale. MPA and Enterprise Singapore (EnterpriseSG), through Singapore Standards Council (SSC), are developing national standards on methanol and also ammonia bunkering. The standards aim to ensure the safe operations and handling of these fuels and will support the maritime industry’s transition to sustainable alternative fuels. They span areas including custody transfer requirements, operational and safety requirements for the delivery of methanol and ammonia from a bunker tanker to receiving vessels, as well as crew training and competencies. The standards for methanol are expected to be published by EnterpriseSG in 2025. MPA’s regulatory framework for methanol bunkering licence is expected to be finalised in the coming months. MPA will call for applications for a licence to supply methanol as a marine fuel in Singapore by the end of the year. 10.  MPA will work closely with the consortiums on the selected chain-of-custody proposals on pilots that assess the feasibility of these approaches and methods, with the aim for further development on a global scale. Next steps for the development of ammonia bunkering capabilities 11.  In March 2024, the world’s first ocean-going ammonia-powered vessel, Fortescue Green Pioneer, successfully conducted its first fuel trial in Singapore4 over a period of six weeks. The Fortescue Green Pioneer received flag approval from the Singapore Registry of Ships (SRS) and the ‘Gas Fuelled Ammonia’ notation by classification society DNV to use ammonia, in combination with diesel, as a marine fuel. A second tranche of three tonnes of liquid ammonia will be loaded for the Fortescue Green Pioneer to conduct further tests and trials over the next few weeks. As part of the line-up of events at Singapore Maritime Week 2024, Fortescue Green Pioneer will be berthed at Keppel Bay. *Analytical inference:* The relevant edge cases are geographic scope questions:

- **Texas-Mexico border operations:** The framework explicitly encompasses international trade and border planning, including the Texas-Mexico Border Transportation Master Plan update (listed as a separate TxDOT planning track). Workspaces with cross-border Mexico operations may find both the TFMP and the Border Transportation Master Plan relevant. *Source: Freight planning page, TxDOT, 2026. https://www.txdot.gov/projects/planning/freight-planning.html.

- **Gulf Intracoastal Waterway:** Listed as a distinct TxDOT freight planning topic alongside the TFMP. Maritime cargo movements on the Gulf Intracoastal Waterway are within TxDOT's freight planning remit via the Maritime programme. *Source: Freight planning page, TxDOT, 2026. https://www.txdot.gov/projects/planning/freight-planning.html.

- **Highway designations:** TxDOT maintains a separate highway designations track and glossary within the freight planning framework, relevant to permitted loads and oversize/overweight movement planning. *Source: Freight planning page, TxDOT, 2026. https://www.txdot.gov/projects/planning/freight-planning.html.

---

## Texas Freight Mobility Plan (Current Operative Plan: 2023 / "Texas Delivers 2050")

The current approved Texas Freight Mobility Plan is hosted by USDOT and identified by the document filename "texas-delivers-2050.pdf." *Source: Texas Freight Plan, U.S. Department of Transportation, updated December 6, 2023. https://www.transportation.gov/mission/office-secretary/office-policy/freight/freight-infrastructure-and-policy/texas-freight-plan.

*Specific content sections of the 2023 TFMP are not available verbatim from the primary source blocks in this corpus. The USDOT page confirms the plan exists and is approved; the document's internal section structure and specific findings are not reproduced in the available source content.*

*Analytical inference:* The 2023 plan, titled "Texas Delivers 2050," established the baseline findings and recommendations that the 2027 update will extend. The 2020 Texas Freight Network Technology and Operations Plan (FNTOP) — which emerged from a major recommendation of the 2018 TFMP — illustrates the trajectory: the TFMP generates programme-level recommendations that then generate standalone operational plans.

## Texas Freight Network Technology and Operations Plan (FNTOP, 2020)

*Analytical inference:* *"The 2018 Texas Freight Mobility Plan (TFMP) provided Texas with a blueprint for facilitating continued economic growth through a comprehensive, multimodal strategy for addressing freight transportation. One major recommendation from the TFMP is for the TxDOT to develop and implement a statewide, technology-based freight safety and operations program... Based on this recommendation, the Freight Planning Branch within TxDOT's (TxDOT) Transportation Planning and Programming Division developed the Texas Freight Network Technology and Operations Plan (FNTOP), which outlines 12 technology based strategies, six of which were advanced to Concept of Operations, to help improve freight transportation safety and mobility in Texas."* *Source: TxDOT Research Library, Texas Freight Network Technology and Operations Plan, 2020. https://library.ctr.utexas.edu/Presto/content/Detail.aspx?ctID=UHVibGljYXRpb25fMTE2MTA%3D&rID=MzM1NDM%3D&ssid=c2NyZWVuSURfMjEzMjI%3D.

*Operational implication:* The FNTOP's 12 technology strategies and 6 Concepts of Operations represent TxDOT's current technology posture for freight safety and mobility. Workspaces operating on Texas corridors should assess which of these strategies — including any related to truck parking availability systems, freight information systems, or connected vehicle technology — are moving toward deployment and could affect their fleet or carrier operations.

## 2027 TFMP Planned Outcomes (Per TxDOT's Published Programme Design)

The 2027 TFMP is structured to produce four categories of output:

- *"Policies: Specific courses of action that, if adopted, will shape the way Texas approaches freight."*
- *"Programs: Collection of initiatives or activities to achieve desired outcomes."*
- *"Technology & Operations: Investments that improve safety and efficiency of existing systems and prepare Texas for the future of freight mobility."*
- *"Projects: Capital investments under development, proposed, and strategic."*

*Source: Texas Freight Mobility Plan page, TxDOT, 2026. https://www.txdot.gov/projects/planning/freight-planning/texas-freight-mobility-plan.html.

*Analytical inference:* The four-category output structure means the 2027 TFMP will simultaneously produce policy recommendations (which shape regulatory and programmatic environment), program designs (which determine funding allocation), technology and operations priorities (which determine what gets deployed on Texas corridors), and project lists (which feed directly into the UTP and STIP). For workspaces with Texas infrastructure dependencies, all four categories are operationally relevant.

## Multimodal Program Architecture (UTP)

The UTP funds five multimodal programme areas relevant to freight:

*"Freight, Trade and Connectivity: Integrating multimodal freight, international trade and corridor planning into TxDOT's statewide planning and project development processes."* *Source: Multimodal transportation programs, TxDOT, 2026. https://www.txdot.gov/projects/planning/utp/multimodal-programs.html.

Additional UTP multimodal programmes with freight relevance: Maritime (port infrastructure and waterway connectivity); Rail (freight and passenger rail system development); Aviation (airport planning and construction); Public Transportation (transit, bicycle and pedestrian). *Source: Multimodal transportation programs, TxDOT, 2026. https://www.txdot.gov/projects/planning/utp/multimodal-programs.html.

## Texas Freight Network Technology and Operations Plan (FNTOP, 2020)

*Analytical inference:* The FNTOP produced 12 technology-based strategies for freight safety and mobility, 6 of which were advanced to Concept of Operations. *"The 2018 Texas Freight Mobility Plan (TFMP) provided Texas with a blueprint for facilitating continued economic growth through a comprehensive, multimodal strategy for addressing freight transportation."* *Source: TxDOT Research Library, Texas Freight Network Technology and Operations Plan, 2020. https://library.ctr.utexas.edu/Presto/content/Detail.aspx?ctID=UHVibGljYXRpb25fMTE2MTA%3D&rID=MzM1NDM%3D&ssid=c2NyZWVuSURfMjEzMjI%3D.

*Analytical inference:* The 6 Concepts of Operations advanced in the FNTOP represent TxDOT's near-term technology deployment candidates for Texas freight corridors. Workspaces operating truck fleets or coordinating road freight on Texas corridors should track which of the 12 strategies (and particularly the 6 COOs) are moving toward implementation — they may affect telematics requirements, parking reservation systems, or corridor data exchange protocols.

## Truck Parking Availability System (TPAS)

TxDOT published a Truck Parking Availability System study in 2024 alongside regional truck parking studies. *Source: Freight planning page, TxDOT, 2026. https://www.txdot.gov/projects/planning/freight-planning.html.

*Analytical inference:* TPAS is directly relevant to workspaces coordinating long-haul road freight on Texas interstate corridors where hours-of-service compliance and safe parking access are operational constraints. If TPAS moves from study to deployed system, it would affect how carrier partners manage Texas corridor runs.

## Economic Role of Freight in Texas (2021)

TxDOT published "The Economic Role of Freight in Texas" in 2021. *Source: Freight planning page, TxDOT, 2026. https://www.txdot.gov/projects/planning/freight-planning.html.

*Analytical inference:* This document provides the quantitative economic baseline for the TFMP's investment justification. Workspaces making client-facing claims about the importance of Texas infrastructure to their supply chains can reference this document as a primary source — though specific figures from it are not available in the corpus source blocks and should be verified directly.

---

The TxDOT freight planning framework does not create a shipper-facing compliance chain in the regulatory sense. It is a state government planning instrument. The relevant chain is an *influence and information* chain:

| Layer | Entity | Role |
|---|---|---|
| Federal | USDOT / FHWA | Approves state freight plans under 49 USC 70202; hosts plans publicly |
| State | TxDOT | Develops and implements the TFMP; administers UTP freight, trade, and connectivity programs |
| Advisory | Texas Freight Advisory Committee (TFAC) | Identifies freight system trends, needs, and issues; guides investment decisions |
| Regional | Metropolitan Planning Organizations (MPOs) / freight advisory committees | Regional input to TFMP stakeholder engagement |
| Private sector | Shippers, carriers, forwarders, port operators, economic development entities | Provide operational intelligence via workshops, interviews, surveys |

*Operational implication:* Workspaces in a freight forwarder, importer, or shipper role sit at the base of this influence chain. Their leverage is exercised through the stakeholder engagement process, TFAC-adjacent participation, and MPO freight committees — not through regulatory compliance filings.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* Whether a specific workspace entity qualifies as a "stakeholder" with formal standing in TFAC proceedings, or whether any formal obligation to participate in TFMP processes attaches to any private-sector entity, requires review against TxDOT's TFAC governance documents and relevant Texas Transportation Code provisions. This brief does not resolve that question.

---

*Note: This section addresses the substantive requirements of the TxDOT freight planning framework as a state government programme — not shipper-facing obligations. Requirements here fall on TxDOT as the plan-producing agency, with participation design elements that affect how private-sector stakeholders can engage.*

## Federal Plan Content Requirements (49 USC 70202)

The TFMP is required to satisfy federal freight plan content requirements under 49 USC 70202 and the Fixing America's Surface Transportation Act. The TxDOT page characterises the plan as required to capture:

*"Texas freight transportation assets, conditions, current and future needs, and economic importance through the lens of critical supply chains as well as broader findings related to freight operations and international trade."* *Source: Texas Freight Mobility Plan page, TxDOT, 2026. https://www.txdot.gov/projects/planning/freight-planning/texas-freight-mobility-plan.html.

*Specific verbatim content requirements from 49 USC 70202 are not reproduced in the available source blocks. The full statutory text is not in the corpus. The above is TxDOT's characterisation of what the plan will capture.*

*Analytical inference:* Federal state freight plan requirements under FAST Act / 49 USC 70202 typically include a description of the state's multimodal freight system, an assessment of the system's ability to support the national freight network, identification of infrastructure needs and financing sources, and performance targets. Workspaces should consult the statutory text directly for the complete list of required plan elements.

## Stakeholder Engagement Design

*"The TFMP will incorporate an active stakeholder engagement process to ensure appropriate representatives are involved in helping identify challenges and solutions to the State's freight mobility. It will feature a multifaceted approach to ensure diverse perspectives, industries, and communities are represented and engaged."*

Engagement channels include: *"the Texas Freight Advisory Committee and Metropolitan Planning Organization freight advisory committees in the state, stakeholder workshops, interviews, project communications, surveys, and project webpage contents."* *Source: Texas Freight Mobility Plan page, TxDOT, 2026. https://www.txdot.gov/projects/planning/freight-planning/texas-freight-mobility-plan.html.

## Texas Freight Advisory Committee Function

*"The Texas Freight Advisory Committee is comprised of diverse expert industry and contributor opinions, who identify significant freight system trends, needs, and issues with respect to the State, that are critical to freight planning. These freight policies, strategies, and performance measures guide the freight-related transportation investment decisions. This long-range planning and coordination, serves as a forum for agency transportation decisions affecting the movement of goods and people."* *Source: Freight planning page, TxDOT, 2026. https://www.txdot.gov/projects/planning/freight-planning.html.

## UTP Freight, Trade and Connectivity Programme

*"Freight, Trade and Connectivity: Integrating multimodal freight, international trade and corridor planning into TxDOT's statewide planning and project development processes."* *Source: Multimodal transportation programs, TxDOT, 2026. https://www.txdot.gov/projects/planning/utp/multimodal-programs.html.

*Analytical inference:* The Freight, Trade and Connectivity programme is the UTP-level instrument through which TFMP recommendations are translated into funded projects and programmes. Workspaces seeking to understand which freight infrastructure investments are actively funded — as opposed to merely planned — should track UTP document library updates and the Statewide Transportation Improvement Program (STIP).

**Effective date:** *Specific [effective date] for the current TFMP cycle not available from primary sources at the time of this authoring pass. The 2023 plan is operative; the 2027 update is in development.*

**Primary deadline:** The 2027 TFMP is scheduled for USDOT approval in early 2027. *Source: Texas Freight Mobility Plan page, TxDOT, 2026. https://www.txdot.gov/projects/planning/freight-planning/texas-freight-mobility-plan.html.

**Jurisdictional scope:** Statewide Texas; multimodal (road, rail, maritime, aviation, pipeline where applicable); with specific sub-regional studies covering Permian Basin, Rio Grande Valley, Gulf Coast/Houston, San Antonio, El Paso/Far West Texas, and Presidio border gateway. *Source: Freight planning page, TxDOT, 2026. https://www.txdot.gov/projects/planning/freight-planning.html.

**Penalty summary:** *Specific [penalty / enforcement provision] not available from primary sources at the time of this authoring pass. The TFMP framework does not create shipper-facing penalties. Federal consequences of Texas failing to maintain an approved plan (under 49 USC 70202) are not described in the available source content.*

---

## What the Framework Is

The TxDOT freight planning framework is Texas's state-level mechanism for satisfying federal freight planning requirements and directing state freight infrastructure investment. It operates through two interlocking instruments:

**Federal statutory basis:** *"TxDOT is developing its 2027 TFMP. This will be the four-year update of its 2023 plan, in accordance with requirements in the Fixing America's Surface Transportation Act and 49 USC 70202."* *Source: Texas Freight Mobility Plan page, TxDOT, 2026. https://www.txdot.gov/projects/planning/freight-planning/texas-freight-mobility-plan.html.

**Programmatic role:** *"TxDOT integrates multimodal freight, trade, and economic considerations into agency-wide planning and programming activities to maintain and improve freight-supportive infrastructure across the state."* *Source: Freight planning page, TxDOT, 2026. https://www.txdot.gov/projects/planning/freight-planning.html.

**Economic scale:** *"If Texas were a nation, it would be the 8th largest economy in the world. It has been the #1 U.S. exporter for 23 years in a row, and it is the largest energy-producing state in the Nation."* *Source: Texas Freight Mobility Plan page, TxDOT, 2026. https://www.txdot.gov/projects/planning/freight-planning/texas-freight-mobility-plan.html.

*"Each year, Texas infrastructure moves billions of tons and trillions of dollars of freight, making Texas an essential link in the global supply chain."* *Source: Freight planning page, TxDOT, 2026. https://www.txdot.gov/projects/planning/freight-planning.html.

## Why It Applies to the Workspace

*Analytical inference:* For any freight forwarder, shipper, importer, distributor, or logistics operator with Texas trade lanes — whether moving cargo through Gulf Coast ports, cross-border at Texas-Mexico gateways, or on Texas highway corridors — the TxDOT freight planning framework shapes the infrastructure investment priorities, truck parking availability, technology deployment programmes, and policy environment that directly affect operational cost, transit reliability, and access to Texas supply chains. The workspace's engagement with this framework is not a compliance obligation in the shipper-facing sense; it is an intelligence and advocacy channel.

*Analytical inference:* For workspaces operating in cargo verticals that depend on Texas intermodal or border infrastructure (including cross-border trade, energy-sector freight, and high-volume road movements), the TFMP's project and policy recommendations — once approved by USDOT — flow into the UTP and STIP, which govern which infrastructure improvements receive state and federal funding over a four-year cycle.

The U.S. DOT hosts the approved 2023 Texas Freight Plan (document: "texas-delivers-2050.pdf") as the current operative plan. *Source: Texas Freight Plan, U.S. Department of Transportation, updated December 6, 2023. https://www.transportation.gov/mission/office-secretary/office-policy/freight/freight-infrastructure-and-policy/texas-freight-plan.

Gaps between the study findings and current operational experience are the substantive input the workspace can contribute to the 2027 TFMP stakeholder process.

## Subscription to TxDOT Freight Updates

TxDOT provides a subscription service (email and SMS/text) for freight planning updates. *Source: Freight planning page, TxDOT, 2026. https://www.txdot.gov/projects/planning/freight-planning.html.

*Analytical inference:* Subscribing to TxDOT freight planning updates is the minimum-cost mechanism for tracking when the 2027 TFMP moves through its development phases and when stakeholder engagement windows open.

## Engagement Protocol for TFMP Process

Establish an internal protocol for the 2027 TFMP stakeholder engagement cycle:

1. **Assess** which Texas corridors and border crossings are operationally material to the workspace.
2. **Map** those corridors against the bottleneck and network assessment scope (Mid 2026 phase).
3. **Verify** whether the workspace or an industry association it belongs to has current representation in TFAC or MPO freight advisory committees.
4. **Engage** TxDOT Freight team to register for stakeholder workshops and supply chain working group participation ahead of the Mid 2026 bottleneck assessment.
