These additional administrative costs are expected to be too small to generate any significant market distortion with social implications (e.g. on consumers or workers). Total regulatory costs are presented in Table 6 with a 3% discount rate. Level playing field The extension of the MRV scope to additional smaller vessels would be expected to have a positive impact on the level playing field by ensuring similar regulatory requirements for vessels just above or below the 5 000 GT threshold, which might be competing for similar market segments. An analysis of vessel data segmented by size suggests that a large proportion of additional vessels under policy scenarios considered would be just below the 5000 GT threshold. Indeed, vessels between 4 000 and 4 999 GT would represent 32% of the considered fleet under scenario A.1, 31% under A.2, and 19% under A.3. 4.5 Comparison of scenarios A in terms of social net present value (different smaller vessels categories in scope assuming no changes in MRV requirements) The social net present value (NPV) across all scenarios considered to expand the scope is negative over the period 2025-2050 (Table 6). This is because the present value of additional administrative costs for companies and authorities is higher than the monetised GHG emission savings solely attributable to the MRV maritime Regulation. However, this NPV calculation should be interpreted cautiously as it does not take into account the possible indirect environmental benefits that would come from the possible subsequent integration of smaller vessels in other GHG mitigation policies, such as the EU ETS and Fuel EU, or any other equivalent measures, following their prior inclusion within MRV scope. It is expected that including costs and benefits from the integration of smaller vessels into EU ETS and/or Fuel EU, in conjunction with MRV, would be showing a very different picture, most likely a positive NPV. Table 6: Social Net Present Value (NPV) of scenarios A.1, A.2 and A.3 compared to the baseline (million EUR over the period 2025-2050) (3% discount rate) Scenario A.1 Scenario A.2 Scenario A.3 GHG emission savings 3.7 4.1 7.5 Regulatory costs -17.6 -17.6 -41.7 Social NPV -13.9 -13.5 -34.2 Source: Ricardo analysis Note: GHG emission savings have been monetised using climate change avoidance cost included in the 2019 Handbook of external costs (EUR 100/tCO 2 e) corrected to 2023 price levels (EUR 133/tCO 2 e by 2030 and EUR 358/tCO 2 e post-2030). 4.6 Impacts from scenario B2 related to changes in monitoring requirements for smaller vessels Removing the threshold of 300 voyages per year (s cenario B.2) would benefit a large proportion of vessels undertaking intra-EU voyages only (32% of total smaller vessels) 30 , significantly expanding the scope of the exemption to report on a per journey basis. Reporting on an aggregate basis, rather than on a per journey basis, could allow companies under this exemption to use simpler monitoring systems (e.g. bunker notes with limited stocktaking), which would be associated with lower monitoring costs. Thus, while no quantitative analysis was performed in relation to this scenario B.2, a qualitative analysis shows that it could allow for a significant reduction in administrative costs compared to scenario B.1. This reduction is not quantified due to lack of quantitative evidence of the difference in costs between monitoring on a per voyage and on an aggregate basis. 5. Conclusions The analysis carried out with regard to GHG emissions from ships below 5 000 gross tonnage but not below 400 gross tonnage confirms that the two ship categories that will be included under the scope of the EU MRV maritime Regulation as from 2025, are actually the ones with the highest emissions within this segment. GHG emissions from smaller vessels in the offshore and general cargo categories represent respectively 22% and 18% of all GHG emissions from smaller vessels. When putting aside emissions from these two categories, total GHG emissions from the remaining smaller vessel categories are estimated at 11.32 MtCO 2 , i.e. 9% of CO 2 emissions covered under MRV in 2023. At the same time, those represent 5 309 vessels, i.e. 42% of the number of vessels that were subject to MRV obligations in 2023. Based on a consultation with representatives of shipping companies, the analysis reveals that recurrent annual MRV-related administrative costs per vessel for smaller vessels would be similar (or slightly higher) than those of larger vessels currently subject to MRV obligations. As a result – and because they emit less GHG emissions than larger vessels – the trade-off between administrative costs for shipping companies and additional monitored GHG emissions would be less favourable for smaller vessels. The ratio between administrative costs and coverage of GHG emissions would be on average seven times higher for smaller vessels, compared to the larger vessels currently subject to MRV obligations. The analysis also reveals that extending the scope of the MRV maritime Regulation to additional categories of smaller vessels would help unlock the implementation of energy efficiency measures and low carbon technologies due to the ability of MRV data to inform decision making process. However, the direct environmental benefits are estimated to be rather small, based on conservative assumptions. In turn, the Social Net Present Value (NPV) is negative for all the considered extension scenarios. It shows that the present value of additional administrative costs for companies and competent authorities is higher than the monetised GHG emission savings solely attributable to the MRV maritime Regulation. However, the picture would look different, with much higher environmental benefits and most likely a positive NPV, when considering the possible indirect benefits that would be associated with GHG emission savings from the possible integration of smaller vessels in other GHG mitigation policies, such as the EU ETS and FuelEU, following their prior inclusion within MRV scope. Related to this, it is worth mentioning that equivalent measures other than integration within FuelEU and/or EU ETS scope might be envisaged – notably if this would enable a reduction of the administrative burden. Such measures could be taken at national level, including for instance taxation-related measures or ‘opt-ins’ within the ‘ETS2’ for buildings, road transport and additional sectors. Some Member States, including Austria, the Netherlands and Sweden, have already decided to include within the scope of ETS2 emissions from some smaller vessels and/or inland navigation. In any case, the additional benefits that could result from integration of smaller vessels in other GHG mitigation policies were not considered in this report, which only deals with the potential inclusion of additional smaller ships within the scope of the MRV maritime Regulation and the direct impacts of such a change. An assessment including such additional benefits will be carried out in the context of the 2026 review of the EU ETS Directive. sections.md:
**Severity: MONITORING.**

No immediate action is required of the workspace by this instrument. The regulation assigns database access and management duties to Member State authorities, shipping companies, verifiers, and the European Commission; freight forwarders and shippers are not among the enumerated user classes (see Threshold Questions).

*Operational implication:* The monitoring posture should watch two things: (a) carrier surcharge and pass-through behaviour as FuelEU penalties and compliance balances become visible to carriers through the database, and (b) any future amendment extending database access or disclosure to commercial counterparties, which would change the workspace's data-access position.

---

| Date | Event | Status |
|---|---|---|
| 13 September 2023 | Parent Regulation (EU) 2023/1805 (FuelEU Maritime) adopted | In force |
| 26 July 2024 | Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2027 on verification activities adopted | In force |
| 24 July 2025 | European Data Protection Supervisor opinion delivered | Completed |
| 23 February 2026 | Commission adopts Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/394 | Adopted |
| 24.2.2026 | Published in the Official Journal (OJ L series 2026/394) | Published |
| Day following publication | Entry into force of this Regulation | In force |

*Sources: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/394. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32026R0394

---

This brief covers Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/394 of 23 February 2026, laying down rules for the application of Regulation (EU) 2023/1805 of the European Parliament and of the Council (FuelEU Maritime) as regards access rights and the functional and technical specifications of the FuelEU database. The instrument specifies who may access the FuelEU database, what each actor may see and manage, and the functional, security, visual, and update requirements of the system that operationalises FuelEU Maritime compliance workflows.

The brief is structured as a Regulatory Fact Document. Sections without grounded content from the source corpus are omitted with an explanatory note. All claims are labelled FACT, ANALYSIS, or LEGAL per the provenance contract. Inline citations are provided at the point of each claim.

**Convention notes:** "The FuelEU database" refers to the electronic database established pursuant to Regulation (EU) 2023/1805. "THETIS-MRV" refers to the automated Union operation system run by EMSA pursuant to Regulation (EU) 2015/757. Quoted passages reproduce the enacted text as published.

---

*No Commission guidance documents interpreting this implementing regulation have been identified in the source corpus as of the date of this brief.* EMSA maintains FuelEU Maritime webinar and tutorial material offering orientation on database workflows. *Source: EMSA FuelEU webinars page, European Maritime Safety Agency. https://www.emsa.europa.eu/reducing-emissions/webinars_and_tutorials/fueleu-webinars.html

---

The regulation maps database rights onto the FuelEU Maritime compliance chain.

FACT: "Access rights and functionalities of the FuelEU database shall correspond to the respective responsibilities of the actors involved in the implementation of Regulation (EU) 2023/1805." *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/394, European Commission, 23 February 2026. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32026R0394

The enumerated user classes are: Member States in four configurations (administering State; flag State; competent authority of the Member State of the port of call; national accreditation body), companies, verifiers, and the European Commission.

FACT: A company holds "access to all information on the ships under its responsibility and previous records, including the FuelEU document of compliance, the FuelEU report and partial FuelEU report, the verification report, the compliance balance, the additional checks report, OPS exceptions". *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/394, European Commission, 23 February 2026. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32026R0394

*Operational implication:* The workspace sits outside this chain, downstream of the "company" actor (the shipowner or ISM company). Any FuelEU compliance evidence the workspace needs from carriers (for example a FuelEU document of compliance) must be requested commercially; the database itself will not provide it to a forwarder.

---

## Union Database Linkage (Renewable Energy Directive)

FACT: To support fuel certification integrity, "the FuelEU database environment shall be connected to the Union Database when its scope and functionalities have been adapted accordingly", referring to the Union Database established under Directive (EU) 2018/2001, so marine bunker fuel compliance can be demonstrated across the supply chain. *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/394, European Commission, 23 February 2026. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32026R0394

*Analytical inference:* This planned linkage points toward end-to-end digital chain-of-custody for marine fuels. For the workspace, carrier claims about renewable or low-carbon fuel use on booked services should, over time, become verifiable against certified records rather than marketing statements.

---

## Reporting Flow Through the Database

Companies report each ship's energy consumption and emissions through the database; verifiers use it for the verification process and issuance of the FuelEU document of compliance; administering authorities access and enter the information needed for their activities.

FACT: "A notification system shall be implemented to inform the company when the verified compliance balance of its ship has been recorded in the FuelEU database." *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/394, European Commission, 23 February 2026. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32026R0394

FACT: "The FuelEU database shall enable the verifier or the administering State as appropriate, to issue the FuelEU document of compliance for the ship concerned, as provided for in Article 22 of Regulation (EU) 2023/1805." For issuance, the verifier provides the required data using an electronic template available in the database. *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/394, European Commission, 23 February 2026. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32026R0394

After verification concludes, compliance balance information is made available by verifiers to the other user classes through the database, and document of compliance information is likewise shared after issuance.

---

## Plain-Language Summary

This implementing regulation is the technical rulebook for the FuelEU database, the central IT system through which FuelEU Maritime compliance is reported, verified, and enforced. It does not create new emissions limits or fuel obligations; those sit in the parent regulation. It determines how the actors already obligated under FuelEU Maritime interact with the compliance infrastructure.

FACT: "This Regulation lays down the rules for access rights and the functional and technical specifications, including notification rules and filtering, of the FuelEU database. It builds upon existing IT systems in the European Maritime Safety Agency (EMSA), mainly THETIS-MRV." *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/394, European Commission, 23 February 2026. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32026R0394

FACT: The regulation is adopted under the parent FuelEU Maritime regulation: "Having regard to Regulation (EU) 2023/1805 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 13 September 2023 on the use of renewable and low-carbon fuels in maritime transport, and amending Directive 2009/16/EC ( 1 ) , and in particular Article 19(3) thereof". *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/394, European Commission, 23 February 2026. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32026R0394

FACT: "The primary foundational structure upon which the FuelEU database is built is THETIS-MRV", the system created to support EU MRV reporting under Regulation (EU) 2015/757, with the aim of capitalising on previously submitted data under a reporting-only-once approach. *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/394, European Commission, 23 February 2026. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32026R0394

FACT: The regulation is directly applicable Union law: "This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States". *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/394, European Commission, 23 February 2026. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32026R0394

FACT: "This Regulation shall enter into force on the day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union"; the Official Journal publication is dated 24.2.2026 (OJ L series 2026/394). *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/394, European Commission, 23 February 2026. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32026R0394

*Operational implication:* The workspace, as a freight forwarder buying ocean freight rather than operating ships, has no direct login, reporting duty, or data-entry obligation in the FuelEU database. Exposure is indirect: carriers' FuelEU compliance costs, penalty pass-throughs, and pooling strategies are administered through this system, and the quality of carrier compliance data offered commercially will reflect the database's verified records.

---

The regulation builds in a controlled evolution path for the database.

FACT: "Specifications for data exchange formats shall be made available no later than 1 month before implementation." Updates and corrections are to be notified to all users prior to implementation through release notes and detailed technical specifications. *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/394, European Commission, 23 February 2026. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32026R0394

EMSA may update functionalities and the interface of the database considering experience gained, technological advancements, evolving user needs, and emerging best practices. A future connection to the Union Database under Directive (EU) 2018/2001 is anticipated (see Adjacent Research section).

---

| # | Title | Issuing Body | Type | URL |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/394 (FuelEU database) | European Commission | Primary legal text | https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32026R0394 |
| 2 | Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/394, Official Journal ELI page | Publications Office of the EU | Primary legal text | https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg_impl/2026/394/oj |
| 3 | FuelEU Maritime policy page | European Commission, DG MOVE | Institutional overview | https://transport.ec.europa.eu/transport-modes/maritime/decarbonising-maritime-transport-fueleu-maritime_en |
| 4 | FuelEU Maritime webinars and tutorials | EMSA | Institutional guidance material | https://www.emsa.europa.eu/reducing-emissions/webinars_and_tutorials/fueleu-webinars.html |
| 5 | FuelEU Maritime full application news item | EMSA | Institutional news | https://www.emsa.europa.eu/newsroom/latest-news/item/5385-fueleu-maritime-full-application-1-january-2025.html |

---

*This section is not applicable to the workspace's profile as a freight forwarder. The regulation specifies compliance infrastructure for ship operators, verifiers, and authorities; it does not regulate products or services sold by the workspace.*

---

## OPS Exceptions and Non-Compliance Records

The database records both exceptions to on-shore power supply obligations and records of non-compliance with those obligations (see Substantive Requirements). These records feed the enforcement workflows of the parent regulation.

## Personal Data

FACT: Processing of personal data in the database is bounded by the GDPR: "The personal data should be kept in a form which permits the identification of data subjects for no longer than necessary for the purposes for which the data were collected". The European Data Protection Supervisor was consulted and delivered an opinion on 24 July 2025. *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/394, European Commission, 23 February 2026. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32026R0394

*Legal Confirmation Required:* Retention periods and data-subject rights for any personnel data a company enters into the database are governed by Regulation (EU) 2016/679 and Regulation (EU) 2018/1725 and should be confirmed by counsel where an affiliated entity acts as a database user.

---

**Q1: Does the workspace have access to the FuelEU database?**

*Per the workspace's reading:* No. The user classes with access rights are exhaustively enumerated as Member State configurations, companies, verifiers, and the European Commission. A freight forwarder that is not the ISM company of a ship is not an enumerated user class, so the workspace neither can nor must register in the database.

**Q2: Does this regulation impose reporting obligations on the workspace?**

*Per the workspace's reading:* No. The reporting, verification, and penalty workflows administered through the database attach to companies, verifiers, and authorities under Regulation (EU) 2023/1805. *Legal Confirmation Required:* If any affiliated entity ever assumes the role of a "company" for a vessel within FuelEU Maritime scope (for example through ship management arrangements), its database obligations under this regulation and the parent regulation should be confirmed by counsel.

---

## Identity, Authentication, and Auditability

The database implements a secure identification mechanism assigning each user a unique ID, with authentication for system-to-system interfaces based on recognised authentication methods, and periodic review of authorisations against access control policies.

FACT: The system ensures non-repudiation of user actions: "the database shall record the user, timestamp and action carried out for any modifications", facilitating auditing and forensic analysis. *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/394, European Commission, 23 February 2026. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32026R0394

## Interfaces and Public Information

A system-to-system interface is defined as an interface for exchanging information in an automated way using a set of predefined messages.

FACT: "All information made publicly available shall be provided in English" to ensure accessibility to a wide audience. *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/394, European Commission, 23 February 2026. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32026R0394

The database is designed to accommodate various screen sizes and viewports, with a non-support message and guidance displayed for incompatible browsers.

---

## Access Model

FACT: "Access rights referred to in paragraph 1 shall be restricted to read-only. Management functionalities referred to in paragraph 1 shall include creating and modifying data." *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/394, European Commission, 23 February 2026. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32026R0394

## On-Shore Power Supply (OPS) Records

FACT: "The FuelEU database shall enable the competent authority of the Member State of the port of call or any duly authorised entity to record exceptions provided for in Article 6(5) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1805", together with records of non-compliance with OPS obligations, using an electronic form available in THETIS-MRV. *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/394, European Commission, 23 February 2026. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32026R0394

## Compliance Balance Management

FACT: "The FuelEU database shall incorporate a compliance balance calculator to enable the company to monitor and manage its compliance balance and to use the flexibility mechanisms provided for in Articles 20 and 21 of Regulation (EU) 2023/1805 as necessary." *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/394, European Commission, 23 February 2026. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32026R0394

The database supports banking of a compliance surplus to the following reporting period and borrowing of an advance compliance surplus from the following reporting period, with company and verifier interacting through the system to request, assess, approve, and record either mechanism.

FACT: "The FuelEU database shall incorporate a pooling functionality that enables companies and verifiers to interact with one another in order to pool the compliance balance of different ships", including registration and verification of the pool composition and allocation. *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/394, European Commission, 23 February 2026. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32026R0394

## Penalty Administration

FACT: "The FuelEU database shall enable the administering state to record and notify to the company the amount of FuelEU penalties applicable to its ships, pursuant to Article 23 of Regulation (EU) 2023/1805." The database also permits registration of proof of penalty payments, and any penalty issued and enforcement action taken by the administering state is automatically recorded. *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/394, European Commission, 23 February 2026. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32026R0394

*Operational implication:* Penalty amounts themselves are set by the parent regulation, not by this instrument; what this instrument does is make penalty issuance, notification, and payment-proof a recorded, auditable database workflow, which increases the traceability of costs carriers may seek to pass through.

---

									<div id="textTabContent">
									
										
	
	
											<div id="document1" class="tabContent">
												<div class="tabContent">
													<div lang="">
														
      <table width="100%" border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0">
         <col width="5%"/>

            <tr>
               <td  >
                  <img alt="European flag" src="./../../../images/europeanflag.gif" height="40pt" width="60pt"/>
               </td>

                  <p class="oj-hd-ti">Official Journal <br/>of the European Union</p>
               </td>

                  <p class="oj-hd-lg">EN</p>

      <hr class="oj-separator"/>
      <table width="100%" border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0">
         <col width="20%"/>
         <col width="60%"/>
         <col width="20%"/>
         <tbody>
            <tr>
               <td  />
               <td  >
                  <p class="oj-hd-uniq">2026/394</p>
               </td>
               <td  >
                  <p class="oj-hd-date">24.2.2026</p>
               </td>
            </tr>
         </tbody>
      </table>
      <div class="eli-container">
         <div class="eli-main-title" id="tit_1">
            <p class="oj-doc-ti" id="d1e43-1-1">
            COMMISSION IMPLEMENTING REGULATION (EU) 2026/394</p>
            <p class="oj-doc-ti">of 23 February 2026
         </p>
            <p class="oj-doc-ti">laying down rules for the application of Regulation (EU) 2023/1805 of the European Parliament and of the Council, as regards access rights and the functional and technical specifications of the FuelEU database</p>
            <p class="oj-doc-ti">(Text with EEA relevance)</p>
         </div>
         <div class="eli-subdivision" id="pbl_1">
            <p class="oj-normal">THE EUROPEAN COMMISSION,</p>
            <div class="eli-subdivision" id="cit_1">
               <p class="oj-normal">Having regard to the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union,</p>
            </div>
            <div class="eli-subdivision" id="cit_2">
               <p class="oj-normal">Having regard to Regulation (EU) 2023/1805 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 13 September 2023 on the use of renewable and low-carbon fuels in maritime transport, and amending Directive 2009/16/EC <a id="ntc1-L_202600394EN.000101-E0001" href="#ntr1-L_202600394EN.000101-E0001"
                     >(<span class="oj-super oj-note-tag">1</span>)</a>, and in particular Article 19(3) thereof,</p>
            </div>
            <p class="oj-normal">Whereas:</p>
            <div class="eli-subdivision" id="rct_1">
               <table width="100%" border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0">
                  <col width="4%"/>
                  <col width="96%"/>
                  <tbody>
                     <tr>
                        <td valign="top"  >
                           <p class="oj-normal">(1)</p>
                        </td>
                        <td valign="top"  >
                           <p class="oj-normal">To increase the consistent use of renewable and low-carbon fuels and substitute sources of energy in maritime transport across the Union, Regulation (EU) 2023/1805 lays down uniform rules imposing a limit on the greenhouse gas intensity of energy used on board a ship arriving at, staying at or departing from ports under the jurisdiction of a Member State, and an obligation to use an on-shore power supply (‘OPS’) or zero-emission technologies at berth in ports under the jurisdiction of a Member State.</p>
                        </td>
                     </tr>
                  </tbody>
               </table>
            </div>
            <div class="eli-subdivision" id="rct_2">
               <table width="100%" border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0">
                  <col width="4%"/>
                  <col width="96%"/>
                  <tbody>
                     <tr>
                        <td valign="top"  >
                           <p class="oj-normal">(2)</p>
                        </td>
                        <td valign="top"  >
                           <p class="oj-normal">To ensure the compliance of monitoring of ships with Regulation (EU) 2023/1805, an electronic database (the ‘FuelEU database’) is to be set up pursuant to that Regulation, which should be used for actions necessary to fulfil the obligations set out in it.</p>
                        </td>
                     </tr>
                  </tbody>
               </table>
            </div>
            <div class="eli-subdivision" id="rct_3">
               <table width="100%" border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0">
                  <col width="4%"/>
                  <col width="96%"/>
                  <tbody>
                     <tr>
                        <td valign="top"  >
                           <p class="oj-normal">(3)</p>
                        </td>
                        <td valign="top"  >
                           <p class="oj-normal">To enable all stakeholders fulfil their obligations set out in Regulation (EU) 2023/1805 in a centralised and harmonised way, the FuelEU database should support: (i) companies in reporting each ships’ energy consumption and emissions; (ii) verifiers in the verification process and issuance of the FuelEU document of compliance; and (iii) the administering authorities in accessing and entering the information needed for their activities.</p>
                        </td>
                     </tr>
                  </tbody>
               </table>
            </div>
            <div class="eli-subdivision" id="rct_4">
               <table width="100%" border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0">
                  <col width="4%"/>
                  <col width="96%"/>
                  <tbody>
                     <tr>
                        <td valign="top"  >
                           <p class="oj-normal">(4)</p>
                        </td>
                        <td valign="top"  >
                           <p class="oj-normal">The objective of the FuelEU database is to significantly alleviate the administrative workload placed on companies, verifiers and other stakeholders. It is built upon the comprehensive network of relevant IT systems, designed to streamline reporting processes within the maritime sector.</p>
                        </td>
                     </tr>
                  </tbody>
               </table>
            </div>
            <div class="eli-subdivision" id="rct_5">
               <table width="100%" border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0">
                  <col width="4%"/>
                  <col width="96%"/>
                  <tbody>
                     <tr>
                        <td valign="top"  >
                           <p class="oj-normal">(5)</p>
                        </td>
                        <td valign="top"  >
                           <p class="oj-normal">The primary foundational structure upon which the FuelEU database is built is THETIS-MRV, which was created to support the implementation of Regulation (EU) 2015/757 of the European Parliament and of the Council <a id="ntc2-L_202600394EN.000101-E0002" href="#ntr2-L_202600394EN.000101-E0002"
                                 >(<span class="oj-super oj-note-tag">2</span>)</a>, with the aim of capitalising on previously submitted data. That strategic approach complies with the ‘reporting only once principle’, fostering synergies between the reporting under Regulations (EU) 2015/757 and (EU) 2023/1805 and ensuring the harmonisation and consistency of information across all operational facets.</p>
                        </td>
                     </tr>
                  </tbody>
               </table>
            </div>
            <div class="eli-subdivision" id="rct_6">
               <table width="100%" border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0">
                  <col width="4%"/>
                  <col width="96%"/>
                  <tbody>
                     <tr>
                        <td valign="top"  >
                           <p class="oj-normal">(6)</p>
                        </td>
                        <td valign="top"  >
                           <p class="oj-normal">In order to be taken into account for the limits set in Article 4 of Regulation (EU) 2023/1805, sustainable marine fuels should be certified in accordance with Article 10 of that Regulation to ensure transparency and mitigate the risk of fraud or erroneous reporting. The Union Database established in accordance with Article 28(2) and (4) of the Directive (EU) 2018/2001 of the European Parliament and of the Council <a id="ntc3-L_202600394EN.000101-E0003" href="#ntr3-L_202600394EN.000101-E0003"
                                 >(<span class="oj-super oj-note-tag">3</span>)</a> could be used to demonstrate the compliance of marine bunker fuels across the whole supply chain. To that end, the FuelEU database environment shall be connected to the Union Database when its scope and functionalities have been adapted accordingly. This will facilitate reporting for companies and support verification activities.</p>
                        </td>
                     </tr>
                  </tbody>
               </table>
            </div>
            <div class="eli-subdivision" id="rct_7">
               <table width="100%" border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0">
                  <col width="4%"/>
                  <col width="96%"/>
                  <tbody>
                     <tr>
                        <td valign="top"  >
                           <p class="oj-normal">(7)</p>
                        </td>
                        <td valign="top"  >
                           <p class="oj-normal">It is necessary to ensure consistency between this Regulation and Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2027 <a id="ntc4-L_202600394EN.000101-E0004" href="#ntr4-L_202600394EN.000101-E0004"
                                 >(<span class="oj-super oj-note-tag">4</span>)</a> in order to streamline verification activities.</p>
                        </td>
                     </tr>
                  </tbody>
               </table>
            </div>
            <div class="eli-subdivision" id="rct_8">
               <table width="100%" border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0">
                  <col width="4%"/>
                  <col width="96%"/>
                  <tbody>
                     <tr>
                        <td valign="top"  >
                           <p class="oj-normal">(8)</p>
                        </td>
                        <td valign="top"  >
                           <p class="oj-normal">When personal data are processed in the context of the application of this Regulation, Regulation (EU) 2016/679 of the European Parliament and of the Council <a id="ntc5-L_202600394EN.000101-E0005" href="#ntr5-L_202600394EN.000101-E0005"
                                 >(<span class="oj-super oj-note-tag">5</span>)</a> applies. The personal data should be kept in a form which permits the identification of data subjects for no longer than necessary for the purposes for which the data were collected <a id="ntc6-L_202600394EN.000101-E0006" href="#ntr6-L_202600394EN.000101-E0006"
                                 >(<span class="oj-super oj-note-tag">6</span>)</a>.</p>
                        </td>
                     </tr>
                  </tbody>
               </table>
            </div>
            <div class="eli-subdivision" id="rct_9">
               <table width="100%" border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0">
                  <col width="4%"/>
                  <col width="96%"/>
                  <tbody>
                     <tr>
                        <td valign="top"  >
                           <p class="oj-normal">(9)</p>
                        </td>
                        <td valign="top"  >
                           <p class="oj-normal">The European Data Protection Supervisor was consulted in accordance with Article 42(1) of Regulation (EU) 2018/1725 of the European Parliament and of the Council <a id="ntc7-L_202600394EN.000101-E0007" href="#ntr7-L_202600394EN.000101-E0007"
                                 >(<span class="oj-super oj-note-tag">7</span>)</a> and delivered an opinion on 24 July 2025.</p>
                        </td>
                     </tr>
                  </tbody>
               </table>
            </div>
            <div class="eli-subdivision" id="rct_10">
               <table width="100%" border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0">
                  <col width="4%"/>
                  <col width="96%"/>
                  <tbody>
                     <tr>
                        <td valign="top"  >
                           <p class="oj-normal">(10)</p>
                        </td>
                        <td valign="top"  >
                           <p class="oj-normal">The measures provided for in this Regulation are in accordance with the opinion of the Committee on Safe Seas and the Prevention of Pollution from Ships,</p>
                        </td>
                     </tr>
                  </tbody>
               </table>
            </div>
            <p class="oj-normal">HAS ADOPTED THIS REGULATION:</p>
         </div>
         <div class="eli-subdivision" id="enc_1">
            <div class="eli-subdivision" id="art_1">
               <p id="d1e228-1-1" class="oj-ti-art">Article 1</p>
               <div class="eli-title" id="art_1.tit_1">
                  <p class="oj-sti-art">Subject matter</p>
               </div>
               <p class="oj-normal">This Regulation lays down the rules for access rights and the functional and technical specifications, including notification rules and filtering, of the FuelEU database. It builds upon existing IT systems in the European Maritime Safety Agency (EMSA), mainly THETIS-MRV.</p>
            </div>
            <div class="eli-subdivision" id="art_2">
               <p id="d1e235-1-1" class="oj-ti-art">Article 2</p>
               <div class="eli-title" id="art_2.tit_1">
                  <p class="oj-sti-art">Definitions</p>
               </div>
               <p class="oj-normal">For the purposes of this Regulation, the following definitions shall apply:</p>
               <table width="100%" border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0">
                  <col width="4%"/>
                  <col width="96%"/>
                  <tbody>
                     <tr>
                        <td valign="top"  >
                           <p class="oj-normal">(1)</p>
                        </td>
                        <td valign="top"  >
                           <p class="oj-normal">‘THETIS-MRV’ means the automated Union operation system run by EMSA pursuant to Regulation (EU) 2015/757;</p>
                        </td>
                     </tr>
                  </tbody>
               </table>
               <table width="100%" border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0">
                  <col width="4%"/>
                  <col width="96%"/>
                  <tbody>
                     <tr>
                        <td valign="top"  >
                           <p class="oj-normal">(2)</p>
                        </td>
                        <td valign="top"  >
                           <p class="oj-normal">‘Authentication’ means authentication as defined in Article 3, point (5), of Regulation (EU) No 910/2014 of the European Parliament and of the Council <a id="ntc8-L_202600394EN.000101-E0008" href="#ntr8-L_202600394EN.000101-E0008"
                                 >(<span class="oj-super oj-note-tag">8</span>)</a>;</p>
                        </td>
                     </tr>
                  </tbody>
               </table>
               <table width="100%" border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0">
                  <col width="4%"/>
                  <col width="96%"/>
                  <tbody>
                     <tr>
                        <td valign="top"  >
                           <p class="oj-normal">(3)</p>
                        </td>
                        <td valign="top"  >
                           <p class="oj-normal">‘System-to-system interface’ means an interface for exchanging information in an automated way using a set of predefined messages.</p>
                        </td>
                     </tr>
                  </tbody>
               </table>
            </div>
            <div class="eli-subdivision" id="art_3">
               <p id="d1e284-1-1" class="oj-ti-art">Article 3</p>
               <div class="eli-title" id="art_3.tit_1">
                  <p class="oj-sti-art">Access rights and management actions</p>
               </div>
               <div id="003.001">
                  <p class="oj-normal">1.   Access rights and functionalities of the FuelEU database shall correspond to the respective responsibilities of the actors involved in the implementation of Regulation (EU) 2023/1805. THETIS-MRV shall have the types of users with the corresponding access rights:</p>
                  <table width="100%" border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0">
                     <col width="4%"/>
                     <col width="96%"/>
                     <tbody>
                        <tr>
                           <td valign="top"  >
                              <p class="oj-normal">(a)</p>
                           </td>
                           <td valign="top"  >
                              <p class="oj-normal">Member States in the following configurations:</p>
                              <table width="100%" border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0">
                                 <col width="4%"/>
                                 <col width="96%"/>
                                 <tbody>
                                    <tr>
                                       <td valign="top"  >
                                          <p class="oj-normal">(1)</p>
                                       </td>
                                       <td valign="top"  >
                                          <p class="oj-normal">Administering State:</p>
                                          <table width="100%" border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0">
                                             <col width="4%"/>
                                             <col width="96%"/>
                                             <tbody>
                                                <tr>
                                                   <td valign="top"  >
                                                      <p class="oj-normal">—</p>
                                                   </td>
                                                   <td valign="top"  >
                                                      <p class="oj-normal">access restricted to information from ships of companies associated with that administering State, including the assessed FuelEU monitoring plan, the verified FuelEU report and partial FuelEU report, the verification report, the verified compliance balance and OPS exceptions and records of non-compliance pursuant to Regulation (EU) 2023/1805;</p>
                                                   </td>
                                                </tr>
                                             </tbody>
                                          </table>
                                          <table width="100%" border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0">
                                             <col width="4%"/>
                                             <col width="96%"/>
                                             <tbody>
                                                <tr>
                                                   <td valign="top"  >
                                                      <p class="oj-normal">—</p>
                                                   </td>
                                                   <td valign="top"  >
                                                      <p class="oj-normal">management of the FuelEU document of compliance pursuant to Article 17(5) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1805, the additional checks report pursuant to Article 17(3) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1805 and the FuelEU penalty-related features pursuant to Article 23(2) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1805.</p>
                                                   </td>
                                                </tr>
                                             </tbody>
                                          </table>
                                       </td>
                                    </tr>
                                 </tbody>
                              </table>
                              <table width="100%" border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0">
                                 <col width="4%"/>
                                 <col width="96%"/>
                                 <tbody>
                                    <tr>
                                       <td valign="top"  >
                                          <p class="oj-normal">(2)</p>
                                       </td>
                                       <td valign="top"  >
                                          <p class="oj-normal">Flag State:</p>
                                          <table width="100%" border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0">
                                             <col width="4%"/>
                                             <col width="96%"/>
                                             <tbody>
                                                <tr>
                                                   <td valign="top"  >
                                                      <p class="oj-normal">—</p>
                                                   </td>
                                                   <td valign="top"  >
                                                      <p class="oj-normal">Access restricted to information related to enforcement actions pursuant to Article 25(3) and Article 25(5) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1805.</p>
                                                   </td>
                                                </tr>
                                             </tbody>
                                          </table>
                                       </td>
                                    </tr>
                                 </tbody>
                              </table>
                              <table width="100%" border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0">
                                 <col width="4%"/>
                                 <col width="96%"/>
                                 <tbody>
                                    <tr>
                                       <td valign="top"  >
                                          <p class="oj-normal">(3)</p>
                                       </td>
                                       <td valign="top"  >
                                          <p class="oj-normal">Competent authority of the Member State of the port of call:</p>
                                          <table width="100%" border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0">
                                             <col width="4%"/>
                                             <col width="96%"/>
                                             <tbody>
                                                <tr>
                                                   <td valign="top"  >
                                                      <p class="oj-normal">—</p>
                                                   </td>
                                                   <td valign="top"  >
                                                      <p class="oj-normal">access restricted to the FuelEU document of compliance;</p>
                                                   </td>
                                                </tr>
                                             </tbody>
                                          </table>
                                          <table width="100%" border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0">
                                             <col width="4%"/>
                                             <col width="96%"/>
                                             <tbody>
                                                <tr>
                                                   <td valign="top"  >
                                                      <p class="oj-normal">—</p>
                                                   </td>
                                                   <td valign="top"  >
                                                      <p class="oj-normal">management of OPS exceptions and records of non-compliance pursuant to Article 6(9) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1805.</p>
                                                   </td>
                                                </tr>
                                             </tbody>
                                          </table>
                                       </td>
                                    </tr>
                                 </tbody>
                              </table>
                              <table width="100%" border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0">
                                 <col width="4%"/>
                                 <col width="96%"/>
                                 <tbody>
                                    <tr>
                                       <td valign="top"  >
                                          <p class="oj-normal">(4)</p>
                                       </td>
                                       <td valign="top"  >
                                          <p class="oj-normal">National accreditation body: access to information on the verifiers that have been accredited by that national accreditation body and ships associated with those verifiers. This information shall include the assessed FuelEU monitoring plan, the verified FuelEU report and partial FuelEU report, the FuelEU document of compliance, the verified compliance balance and the additional checks report.</p>
                                       </td>
                                    </tr>
                                 </tbody>
                              </table>
                           </td>
                        </tr>
                     </tbody>
                  </table>
                  <table width="100%" border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0">
                     <col width="4%"/>
                     <col width="96%"/>
                     <tbody>
                        <tr>
                           <td valign="top"  >
                              <p class="oj-normal">(b)</p>
                           </td>
                           <td valign="top"  >
                              <p class="oj-normal">Company:</p>
                              <table width="100%" border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0">
                                 <col width="4%"/>
                                 <col width="96%"/>
                                 <tbody>
                                    <tr>
                                       <td valign="top"  >
                                          <p class="oj-normal">—</p>
                                       </td>
                                       <td valign="top"  >
                                          <p class="oj-normal">access to all information on the ships under its responsibility and previous records, including the FuelEU document of compliance, the FuelEU report and partial FuelEU report, the verification report, the compliance balance, the additional checks report, OPS exceptions;</p>
                                       </td>
                                    </tr>
                                 </tbody>
                              </table>
                              <table width="100%" border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0">
                                 <col width="4%"/>
                                 <col width="96%"/>
                                 <tbody>
                                    <tr>
                                       <td valign="top"  >
                                          <p class="oj-normal">—</p>
                                       </td>
                                       <td valign="top"  >
                                          <p class="oj-normal">access to information related to the company’s own ships on the pooling of compliance arrangements pursuant to Article 21 of Regulation (EU) 2023/1805;</p>
                                       </td>
                                    </tr>
                                 </tbody>
                              </table>
                              <table width="100%" border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0">
                                 <col width="4%"/>
                                 <col width="96%"/>
                                 <tbody>
                                    <tr>
                                       <td valign="top"  >
                                          <p class="oj-normal">—</p>
                                       </td>
                                       <td valign="top"  >
                                          <p class="oj-normal">management of the ship and company data, and the monitoring plan pursuant to Articles 7 and 8 of Regulation (EU) 2023/1805 respectively.</p>
                                       </td>
                                    </tr>
                                 </tbody>
                              </table>
                           </td>
                        </tr>
                     </tbody>
                  </table>
                  <table width="100%" border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0">
                     <col width="4%"/>
                     <col width="96%"/>
                     <tbody>
                        <tr>
                           <td valign="top"  >
                              <p class="oj-normal">(c)</p>
                           </td>
                           <td valign="top"  >
                              <p class="oj-normal">Verifier:</p>
                              <table width="100%" border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0">
                                 <col width="4%"/>
                                 <col width="96%"/>
                                 <tbody>
                                    <tr>
                                       <td valign="top"  >
                                          <p class="oj-normal">—</p>
                                       </td>
                                       <td valign="top"  >
                                          <p class="oj-normal">access to all information on the ships under its responsibility, previous records and information on all ships in the compliance pool where the verifier is selected to verify the pool compliance;</p>
                                       </td>
                                    </tr>
                                 </tbody>
                              </table>
                              <table width="100%" border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0">
                                 <col width="4%"/>
                                 <col width="96%"/>
                                 <tbody>
                                    <tr>
                                       <td valign="top"  >
                                          <p class="oj-normal">—</p>
                                       </td>
                                       <td valign="top"  >
                                          <p class="oj-normal">management of the monitoring plan, FuelEU report and partial FuelEU report, verification report, FuelEU document of compliance, compliance balance, additional checks report, if authorised by the administering State to conduct such checks on its behalf, and OPS exceptions pursuant to Regulation (EU) 2023/1805.</p>
                                       </td>
                                    </tr>
                                 </tbody>
                              </table>
                           </td>
                        </tr>
                     </tbody>
                  </table>
                  <table width="100%" border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0">
                     <col width="4%"/>
                     <col width="96%"/>
                     <tbody>
                        <tr>
                           <td valign="top"  >
                              <p class="oj-normal">(d)</p>
                           </td>
                           <td valign="top"  >
                              <p class="oj-normal">European Commission:</p>
                              <table width="100%" border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0">
                                 <col width="4%"/>
                                 <col width="96%"/>
                                 <tbody>
                                    <tr>
                                       <td valign="top"  >
                                          <p class="oj-normal">—</p>
                                       </td>
                                       <td valign="top"  >
                                          <p class="oj-normal">access to the following assessed and verified information for the sole purpose to use the data in aggregate form for the future evaluation of the functioning of Regulation (EU) 2023/1805: the verified FuelEU reports and partial FuelEU reports, for the management reports referred to in Article 5(2) and 30(2) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1805, FuelEU documents of compliance, the verified compliance balance, the additional checks reports and OPS exceptions.</p>
                                       </td>
                                    </tr>
                                 </tbody>
                              </table>
                           </td>
                        </tr>
                     </tbody>
                  </table>
               </div>
               <div id="003.002">
                  <p class="oj-normal">2.   Access rights referred to in paragraph 1 shall be restricted to read-only. Management functionalities referred to in paragraph 1 shall include creating and modifying data.</p>
               </div>
            </div>
            <div class="eli-subdivision" id="art_4">
               <p id="d1e396-1-1" class="oj-ti-art">Article 4</p>
               <div class="eli-title" id="art_4.tit_1">
                  <p class="oj-sti-art">Connection to on-shore power supply</p>
               </div>
               <p class="oj-normal">The FuelEU database shall enable the competent authority of the Member State of the port of call or any duly authorised entity to record exceptions provided for in Article 6(5) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1805 (‘OPS exceptions’) and records of non-compliance with on-shore power supply (OPS) obligations pursuant to Article 6(9) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1805 using an electronic form available in THETIS-MRV.</p>
            </div>
            <div class="eli-subdivision" id="art_5">
               <p id="d1e407-1-1" class="oj-ti-art">Article 5</p>
               <div class="eli-title" id="art_5.tit_1">
                  <p class="oj-sti-art">Management of the compliance balance and FuelEU penalties</p>
               </div>
               <div id="005.001">
                  <p class="oj-normal">1.   The FuelEU database shall incorporate a functionality for the management of monitoring plans, including their submissions and modifications.</p>
               </div>
               <div id="005.002">
                  <p class="oj-normal">2.   The FuelEU database shall incorporate a compliance balance calculator to enable the company to monitor and manage its compliance balance and to use the flexibility mechanisms provided for in Articles 20 and 21 of Regulation (EU) 2023/1805 as necessary.</p>
               </div>
               <div id="005.003">
                  <p class="oj-normal">3.   For the purpose of calculating or recording the ship-specific compliance balance referred to in Article 16(4), point (b) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1805, the FuelEU database shall make an electronic template available.</p>
               </div>
               <div id="005.004">
                  <p class="oj-normal">4.   The FuelEU database shall enable the company and the verifier to interact with one another in order to request, assess, approve and record either of the following:</p>
                  <table width="100%" border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0">
                     <col width="4%"/>
                     <col width="96%"/>
                     <tbody>
                        <tr>
                           <td valign="top"  >
                              <p class="oj-normal">(a)</p>
                           </td>
                           <td valign="top"  >
                              <p class="oj-normal">the banking of the compliance surplus to the following reporting period;</p>
                           </td>
                        </tr>
                     </tbody>
                  </table>
                  <table width="100%" border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0">
                     <col width="4%"/>
                     <col width="96%"/>
                     <tbody>
                        <tr>
                           <td valign="top"  >
                              <p class="oj-normal">(b)</p>
                           </td>
                           <td valign="top"  >
                              <p class="oj-normal">the borrowing of an advance compliance surplus from the following reporting period as provided for in Article 20(1) and 20(3) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1805.</p>
                           </td>
                        </tr>
                     </tbody>
                  </table>
               </div>
               <div id="005.005">
                  <p class="oj-normal">5.   The FuelEU database shall incorporate a pooling functionality that enables companies and verifiers to interact with one another in order to pool the compliance balance of different ships and to register and verify the composition of the pool and the allocation of the pool’s compliance balance to each ship, as provided for in Article 21 of Regulation (EU) 2023/1805.</p>
               </div>
               <div id="005.006">
                  <p class="oj-normal">6.   A notification system shall be implemented to inform the company when the verified compliance balance of its ship has been recorded in the FuelEU database.</p>
               </div>
               <div id="005.007">
                  <p class="oj-normal">7.   After the conclusion of the verification of compliance balance by the verifier, the information on the compliance balance shall be made available by verifiers to other users referred to in Article 3 of this Regulation through the FuelEU database.</p>
               </div>
               <div id="005.008">
                  <p class="oj-normal">8.   The FuelEU database shall enable the administering state to record and notify to the company the amount of FuelEU penalties applicable to its ships, pursuant to Article 23 of Regulation (EU) 2023/1805. The FuelEU database shall permit the registration of the proof of the payments of the FuelEU penalties by the entities that made that payment. Any penalty issued and enforcement action taken by the administering state shall be automatically recorded in the FuelEU database.</p>
               </div>
            </div>
            <div class="eli-subdivision" id="art_6">
               <p id="d1e466-1-1" class="oj-ti-art">Article 6</p>
               <div class="eli-title" id="art_6.tit_1">
                  <p class="oj-sti-art">FuelEU document of compliance</p>
               </div>
               <div id="006.001">
                  <p class="oj-normal">1.   The FuelEU database shall enable the verifier or the administering State as appropriate, to issue the FuelEU document of compliance for the ship concerned, as provided for in Article 22 of Regulation (EU) 2023/1805. For the purposes of issuing the FuelEU document of compliance, the verifier shall provide the data required using an electronic template available in the FuelEU database.</p>
               </div>
               <div id="006.002">
                  <p class="oj-normal">2.   After the issuance of the document of compliance by the verifier, the information on the document of compliance shall be made available by verifiers to other users referred to for in Article 3 of this Regulation through the FuelEU database.</p>
               </div>
            </div>
            <div class="eli-subdivision" id="art_7">
               <p id="d1e481-1-1" class="oj-ti-art">Article 7</p>
               <div class="eli-title" id="art_7.tit_1">
                  <p class="oj-sti-art">Security</p>
               </div>
               <div id="007.001">
                  <p class="oj-normal">1.   A secure identification mechanism shall be implemented in the FuelEU database to identify unique users and assign each user a unique ID.</p>
               </div>
               <div id="007.002">
                  <p class="oj-normal">2.   The authentication process for system-to-system interfaces accessing the FuelEU database shall be based on recognised authentication methods, ensuring the integrity and security of data exchanges.</p>
               </div>
               <div id="007.003">
                  <p class="oj-normal">3.   Users accessing the FuelEU database shall be authorised based on access control measures, regulating their access to information and functionalities within the database as provided for in Article 3 of this Regulation.</p>
               </div>
               <div id="007.004">
                  <p class="oj-normal">4.   Authorisations granted to users shall be periodically reviewed to ensure compliance with access control policies and to adapt to any changes in user roles and responsibilities.</p>
               </div>
               <div id="007.005">
                  <p class="oj-normal">5.   The FuelEU database shall ensure non-repudiation of actions performed by users through its interfaces. For this purpose, the database shall record the user, timestamp and action carried out for any modifications, facilitating auditing and a forensic analysis of user activities.</p>
               </div>
            </div>
            <div class="eli-subdivision" id="art_8">
               <p id="d1e511-1-1" class="oj-ti-art">Article 8</p>
               <div class="eli-title" id="art_8.tit_1">
                  <p class="oj-sti-art">Visual requirements</p>
               </div>
               <div id="008.001">
                  <p class="oj-normal">1.   The FuelEU database shall be designed to accommodate various screen sizes and viewports to ensure optimal accessibility for users.</p>
               </div>
               <div id="008.002">
                  <p class="oj-normal">2.   In the event of a user accessing a web page using a non-compatible browser, a ‘non-support’ message shall be displayed, informing the user of the browser’s incompatibility and providing guidance on alternative browsers that support the content.</p>
               </div>
               <div id="008.003">
                  <p class="oj-normal">3.   All information made publicly available shall be provided in English to ensure that it is accessible and understandable to a wide audience.</p>
               </div>
            </div>
            <div class="eli-subdivision" id="art_9">
               <p id="d1e535-1-1" class="oj-ti-art">Article 9</p>
               <div class="eli-title" id="art_9.tit_1">
                  <p class="oj-sti-art">System updates</p>
               </div>
               <div id="009.001">
                  <p class="oj-normal">1.   EMSA may update functionalities and the interface of the FuelEU database if necessary, considering the experience gained, technological advancements, evolving user needs and emerging best practices in web accessibility and usability.</p>
               </div>
               <div id="009.002">
                  <p class="oj-normal">2.   Updates and corrections shall be notified to all users prior to implementation to allow for a timely adjustment of any supporting systems or procedures and clearly communicated to all users through release notes and detailed technical specifications. Specifications for data exchange formats shall be made available no later than 1 month before implementation.</p>
               </div>
            </div>
            <div class="eli-subdivision" id="art_10">
               <p id="d1e550-1-1" class="oj-ti-art">Article 10</p>
               <div class="eli-title" id="art_10.tit_1">
                  <p class="oj-sti-art">Entry into force</p>
               </div>
               <p class="oj-normal">This Regulation shall enter into force on the day following that of its publication in the <span class="oj-italic">Official Journal of the European Union</span>.</p>
            </div>
         </div>
         <div class="eli-subdivision" id="fnp_1">
            <div class="oj-final">
               <p class="oj-normal">This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States.</p>
               <p class="oj-normal">Done at Brussels, 23 February 2026.</p>
               <div class="oj-signatory">
                  <p class="oj-signatory">
                     <span class="oj-italic">For the Commission</span>
                  </p>
                  <p class="oj-signatory">
                     <span class="oj-italic">The President</span>
                  </p>
                  <p class="oj-signatory">Ursula VON DER LEYEN
            </p>
               </div>
            </div>
         </div>
